paragraphs.signature: 玩家在开始前写下一条规则：只要赢到一元钱，就离开牌桌。
他没有要求硬币改变概率，也没有预知下一步。他只改变了记账的时刻。若游戏可以永远继续，第一次赢钱似乎迟早会到来；到那时再清点本钱，结局便不再像一个平均收益为零的实验。
第十五章中，每一步的公平已经能够约束路径的振荡。但玩家选择的终点，是由这条路径自己决定的。固定时刻的条件平均，能否穿过这样的选择，需要重新证明。
本章先固定离散时间滤过 MATHINLINE"(\\mathcal F_n)_{n\\ge0}"。取值于 MATHINLINE"\\mathbb N_0\\cup\\{\\infty\\}" 的随机变量 MATHINLINE"T" 称为停止时刻，如果
MATHBLOCK"\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n\\qquad(n\\ge0)."
这说的不是玩家在时刻零就知道什么时候离开，而是在时刻 MATHINLINE"n" 能够知道自己是否已经离开。等价地，MATHINLINE"\\{T=n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n"：一个方向取相邻差，另一个方向取有限并。于是 MATHINLINE"\\{T\\ge k\\}\\in\\mathcal F_{k-1}"。这最后一个事件会成为合法下注的指标。

设 MATHINLINE"S_n" 是简单对称随机游走。第一次到达1的时间是停止时刻，因为“截至现在是否到过1”只使用已经出现的步子。相反，在固定期限 MATHINLINE"N" 内最后一次到达0的时刻一般不是停止时刻：刚在0的位置离开以后，必须看见未来才能知道这是不是最后一次。具体地取 MATHINLINE"N=2"，最后一个零点 MATHINLINE"L" 满足 MATHINLINE"\\{L=0\\}=\\{S_2\\ne0\\}"，它不是平凡的 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_0" 中的事件。
随机时间与停止时刻的区别，因而是信息上的区别，而不是时间是否随机的区别。
在可能无穷的停止时刻处，定义
MATHBLOCK"\\mathcal F_T=\\{A\\in\\mathcal F:\\ A\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n\\text{ for every }n\\}."
这里原概率空间的 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F" 必须保留：规则没有约束 MATHINLINE"\\{T=\\infty\\}" 上的信息。有限时间片上的等价条件是 MATHINLINE"A\\cap\\{T=n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n"。通过取补集和可数并，立即验证这确实是σ-代数；MATHINLINE"T" 对它可测。
若 MATHINLINE"S\\le T"，则 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_S\\subseteq\\mathcal F_T"。事实上
MATHBLOCK"A\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}=(A\\cap\\{S\\le n\\})\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n."

若 MATHINLINE"X_n" 适应，且先约定在 MATHINLINE"T=\\infty" 上取一个确定值0，那么 MATHINLINE"X_T" 对 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_T" 可测：在 MATHINLINE"\\{T\\le n\\}" 上，它是有限个 MATHINLINE"X_k\\mathbf1_{\\{T=k\\}}" 的拼接。这个约定并不声称0是过程在无穷远的极限。以后只有在已经证明终值存在时，才另行使用那个终值。
停止时刻的最小值、最大值仍是停止时刻。若 MATHINLINE"S\\le T"，还可验证 MATHINLINE"A\\in\\mathcal F_S" 蕴含 MATHINLINE"A\\cap\\{S<k\\le T\\}\\in\\mathcal F_{k-1}"。这正是从 MATHINLINE"S" 开始、到 MATHINLINE"T" 结束的一段账本所需的信息。
令 MATHINLINE"X^T_n=X_{n\\wedge T}"。它适应，因为可按 MATHINLINE"T=0,\\ldots,n-1" 与 MATHINLINE"T\\ge n" 分片。对可积过程，有限拼接仍可积。更重要的是逐条路径恒等式
MATHBLOCK"X^T_n=X_0+\\sum_{k=1}^n\\mathbf1_{\\{T\\ge k\\}}(X_k-X_{k-1})."
第 MATHINLINE"k" 次增量是否记入，在它发生前已经确定。因此若 MATHINLINE"X" 是鞅，条件平均给出 MATHINLINE"X^T" 仍是鞅；次鞅、上鞅分别保留自己的不等号。这里没有关于随机时间的定理作前提，只有有限求和。
同一计算也适用于任意有界的、MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_{k-1}"-可测的下注额 MATHINLINE"H_k"。鞅增量乘以这种预先决定的因子，有限和仍为鞅。对于次鞅和上鞅，保留不等号还要求 MATHINLINE"H_k\\ge0"。无限次下注的可积性却不能由这个有限事实自动获得。
![路径在第7步首次命中高度3。停止路径此前与原路径相同，此后恒为3；原路径继续上下运动。](../assets/visuals/batch16-20/stopping-prefix.zh.svg)
首次到达只使用已经发生的记录。固定近邻路径在第7步首次达到高度3；实线保留停止前缀，方形点虚线在此后冻结为3，细点线显示未停止的原路径。这里没有随机抽样，有限路径示意不是可选抽样定理的证明，也不保证任意停止规则保持期望。
[SVG 静态图](../assets/visuals/batch16-20/stopping-prefix.zh.svg) · [矢量 PDF](../assets/visuals/batch16-20/stopping-prefix.zh.pdf)
设 MATHINLINE"M" 是鞅，MATHINLINE"S\\le T\\le N" 为停止时刻。我们要证明的不是只有总期望相等，而是
MATHBLOCK"\\mathbb E[M_T\\mid\\mathcal F_S]=M_S."
对 MATHINLINE"A\\in\\mathcal F_S"，写出
MATHBLOCK"\\mathbb E[(M_T-M_S)\\mathbf1_A]\n=\\sum_{k=1}^N\\mathbb E[\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{S<k\\le T\\}}(M_k-M_{k-1})]=0."
每个指标均对 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_{k-1}" 可测；每个乘积可积。上节的可测性说明 MATHINLINE"M_S" 属于 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_S"，因此这正是条件期望的定义。对次鞅同一求和给出 ≥0，对上鞅给出 ≤0。
这便是有界停止时刻的可选抽样。它没有要求 MATHINLINE"S,T" 与过程独立，反而容许玩家充分使用过去。真正起作用的，是不许使用尚未发生的增量，以及总共只清算有限笔可积的账。
从整数 MATHINLINE"x\\in\\{1,\\ldots,a-1\\}" 出发，每步以概率 MATHINLINE"p\\in(0,1)" 向右、以 MATHINLINE"q=1-p" 向左，记首次到达0或 MATHINLINE"a" 的时间为 MATHINLINE"T"。不能先写 MATHINLINE"S_T" 再默认它存在。
任意尚未吸收的位置，接下来 MATHINLINE"a" 步若全向右便会吸收，其条件概率至少 MATHINLINE"p^a"。分块迭代得到
MATHBLOCK"P_x(T>ka)\\le(1-p^a)^k."
因此 MATHINLINE"T<\\infty" 几乎必然，而且 MATHINLINE"E_xT<\\infty"。在公平情形 MATHINLINE"p=q=1/2"，对 MATHINLINE"T\\wedge n" 使用有界抽样，MATHINLINE"E_xS_{T\\wedge n}=x"。停止后的路径被0与 MATHINLINE"a" 控制，DCT给出
MATHBLOCK"P_x(S_T=a)=x/a."
期限随机，但清算前后的本钱都有同一个确定上界，这才使极限安全地通过期望。
公平游走满足 MATHINLINE"S_n^2-n" 为鞅：展开平方，条件交叉项为0、增量平方为1。对有界时刻应用刚才已经证明的抽样，得到
MATHBLOCK"E_x(T\\wedge n)=E_xS_{T\\wedge n}^2-x^2."
左边单调趋于 MATHINLINE"E_xT"，右边由有界收敛趋于 MATHINLINE"a^2(x/a)-x^2"。所以
MATHBLOCK"E_xT=x(a-x)."
对于 MATHINLINE"p\\ne q"，取 MATHINLINE"r=q/p"。因为 MATHINLINE"pr+q/r=1"，MATHINLINE"r^{S_n}" 是鞅。停止在有限区间内仍被确定常数控制，故
MATHBLOCK"P_x(S_T=a)=\\frac{1-r^x}{1-r^a}."
它在 MATHINLINE"p\\to1/2" 时趋于 MATHINLINE"x/a"。漂移改变的是调和读数：公平时位置本身足够，偏向一侧时指数函数才消掉平均漂移。
从0出发的公平游走，令 MATHINLINE"T" 为首次到达1的时间。在区间 MATHINLINE"[-a,1]" 使用上节的有限区间公式，先到1的概率为 MATHINLINE"a/(a+1)"，所以 MATHINLINE"P(T<\\infty)=1"。可是
MATHBLOCK"E S_{T\\wedge n}=0,\\qquad S_{T\\wedge n}\\longrightarrow S_T=1\\quad\\text{a.s.}"
这不是停止时刻不合法，而是有限清算的极限不满足一致可积性。
还可证明 MATHINLINE"ET=\\infty"。如果 MATHINLINE"ET<\\infty"，由于步长绝对值为1，
MATHBLOCK"|S_T-S_{T\\wedge n}|\\le(T-n)^+,"
右边期望趋0，于是左边在 MATHINLINE"L^1" 中趋0，迫使 MATHINLINE"ES_T=0"，与 MATHINLINE"S_T=1" 矛盾。因此“几乎必然能等到”与“等待有有限平均代价”是不同命题。
另一个玩家第一次押1，输了押2，再输押4，直到第一次赢。令 MATHINLINE"\\varepsilon_k" 为独立的 ±1 公平结果，MATHINLINE"T" 为首次正面，净收益为
MATHBLOCK"G_n=\\sum_{k=1}^{n}2^{k-1}\\mathbf1_{\\{T\\ge k\\}}\\varepsilon_k."
每个有限期限它都是可积鞅，MATHINLINE"EG_n=0"。第一次赢以前累计损失为 MATHINLINE"-(2^n-1)"，一旦赢则净赚1。因此 MATHINLINE"T<\\infty" 几乎必然，MATHINLINE"G_T=1"，但 MATHINLINE"G_{T\\wedge n}=G_n" 不一致可积。
这里 MATHINLINE"ET=2" 甚至有限。故单独要求停止时间可积仍不够：刚才一步绝对值≤1的控制，这里已经失效。有限期限公平、可积的等待时间、几乎必然赢钱，三件事可以同时发生；代价是没有统一控制的损失与下注额。

第十五章证明，一致可积鞅恰好可写成 MATHINLINE"M_n=E[Z\\mid\\mathcal F_n]"，其中 MATHINLINE"Z\\in L^1"。令 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_\\infty=\\sigma(\\bigcup_n\\mathcal F_n)"，取已证明存在的 MATHINLINE"M_\\infty=E[Z\\mid\\mathcal F_\\infty]"。在 MATHINLINE"T=\\infty" 上使用这个终值。
对任意停止时刻 MATHINLINE"T"，将 MATHINLINE"A\\in\\mathcal F_T" 按 MATHINLINE"T=k" 分片，并用条件期望定义，得到
MATHBLOCK"E[M_T\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T<\\infty\\}}]\n=E[Z\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T<\\infty\\}}]."
绝对可积性也不能省略：逐片先用 MATHINLINE"E[|M_k|\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T=k\\}}]\\le E[|Z|\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T=k\\}}]"，再求和。在无穷时间片，若原 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F" 比 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_\\infty" 更大，不能自动得到同样等式。

不过，抽样定理本身不需要缩小原来的 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F"。改用规范终值 MATHINLINE"M_\\infty"：第十五章已给出 MATHINLINE"M_k=E[M_\\infty\\mid\\mathcal F_k]"。对有限时间片作同一求和，在 MATHINLINE"T=\\infty" 片上则两边的被积变量本来就都是 MATHINLINE"M_\\infty"，不要求该片中的事件属于 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_\\infty"。有限片的绝对积分和不超过 MATHINLINE"E|M_\\infty|"，无穷片也可积，因此确有 MATHINLINE"M_T=E[M_\\infty\\mid\\mathcal F_T]"。若在下面第一式中取 MATHINLINE"Z=M_\\infty"，再用 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_S\\subseteq\\mathcal F_T" 的塔式法则，便得到
MATHBLOCK"M_T=E[Z\\mid\\mathcal F_T],\\qquad\nE[M_T\\mid\\mathcal F_S]=M_S\\quad(S\\le T)."

这允许 MATHINLINE"S\\le T" 都取∞，终值始终按 MATHINLINE"M_\\infty" 约定。若仍保留最初任意的闭合变量 MATHINLINE"Z"，则第一式还需要无穷片上的额外条件；例如 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F=\\mathcal F_\\infty" 足够，而几乎必然有限的 MATHINLINE"T" 也不受这个问题影响。差别不是形式上的：取所有 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_n" 平凡、MATHINLINE"Z" 为等概率的±1隐变量、MATHINLINE"T\\equiv\\infty"，便有 MATHINLINE"M_T=M_\\infty=0"，而原环境中的 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_T=\\mathcal F" 使 MATHINLINE"E[Z\\mid\\mathcal F_T]=Z"。失效的是任意闭合变量的公式，不是规范终值下的抽样结论。

可以。对一个几乎必然有限的 MATHINLINE"T"，若停止族 MATHINLINE"\\{M_{n\\wedge T}:n\\ge0\\}" 一致可积，第十五章说明它在 MATHINLINE"L^1" 中趋于 MATHINLINE"M_T"。于是 MATHINLINE"EM_T=EM_0"。更一般，MATHINLINE"S\\le T" 时，停止鞅已闭合，由上节得到 MATHINLINE"E[M_T\\mid\\mathcal F_S]=M_S"。这是对实际采用规则的局部条件，不必控制停止以后的全部游戏。

停止族条件也允许 MATHINLINE"T=\\infty"。令 MATHINLINE"N_n=M_{n\\wedge T}"，其一致可积性给出可积终值 MATHINLINE"Y" 及 MATHINLINE"N_n=E[Y\\mid\\mathcal F_n]"。在 MATHINLINE"T<\\infty" 上，路径最终固定，故 MATHINLINE"Y=M_T"；在无穷片上用 MATHINLINE"Y" 定义清算值。对 MATHINLINE"S\\le T"，将16.9用于这个停止过程，便得 MATHINLINE"E[Y\\mid\\mathcal F_S]=M_S"，其中 MATHINLINE"S=\\infty" 时也取 MATHINLINE"Y"。这不要求原过程在整个空间上已有一个无穷远终值。
一种易检查的充分条件是 MATHINLINE"ET<\\infty"，并且 MATHINLINE"|M_k-M_{k-1}|\\le C" 几乎必然。此时
MATHBLOCK"|M_{n\\wedge T}|\\le|M_0|+CT\\in L^1,"
故停止族一致可积。有限区间赌博则由停止位置有界获得同一条件。两种控制并不相同，却都明确限制了极限可能藏匿的尾部。
对于非负上鞅与几乎必然有限的 MATHINLINE"T"，有界抽样及Fatou只给出 MATHINLINE"EM_T\\le EM_0"，一般不能把不等号升成等号。若整个上鞅已一致可积，或相应停止族一致可积，可按相同极限程序保留适当的条件不等式。
对适应的离散过程及可测状态集合 MATHINLINE"B"，定义 MATHINLINE"T_B=\\inf\\{n\\ge0:X_n\\in B\\}"，约定空集的下确界为∞。因为
MATHBLOCK"\\{T_B\\le n\\}=\\bigcup_{k=0}^n\\{X_k\\in B\\},"
它总是停止时刻；从时刻1开始的首次返回也一样。若从停止时刻 MATHINLINE"S" 以后再寻找一次命中，事件按 MATHINLINE"S=k\\le n" 分片、再取有限并，仍然只使用截至 MATHINLINE"n" 的信息。
这解释了为什么返回可以反复使用，却没有假定“每次回来以后都独立重来”。停止时刻只保证规则合法，重新开始的分布是否仅由当前位置决定，是下一种额外结构的问题。
第四章的粒子并不只在整数时刻出现。本章的离散定理不能直接代替连续时间抽样，但可以先清楚建立一个可测性事实。
设 MATHINLINE"X_t" 是度量空间中的连续适应过程，MATHINLINE"C" 为闭集。对固定 MATHINLINE"t"，连续性与区间紧性给出
MATHBLOCK"\\{T_C\\le t\\}=\\left\\{\\inf_{s\\in([0,t]\\cap\\mathbb Q)\\cup\\{t\\}}d(X_s,C)=0\\right\\}\\in\\mathcal F_t."

所以首次命中闭集合法。若仅有右连续路径，对开集 MATHINLINE"O" 则先有 MATHINLINE"\\{T_O<t\\}=\\bigcup_{r\\in\\mathbb Q,\\,0\\le r<t}\\{X_r\\in O\\}"。在右连续滤过下，MATHINLINE"\\{T_O\\le t\\}=\\bigcap_m\\{T_O<t+1/m\\}\\in\\mathcal F_t"。这些证明只处理所列路径类别与集合类别。
右连续路径碰闭集不能照抄第一个证明：路径可能在1以前趋近0，却在1跳到1，其距离下确界为0而没有碰到0。一般début定理还涉及更深的可测投影；本章没有把它当成显然，也没有假定任意鞅已经有右连续版本。连续时间抽样、通常条件与正则化仍须在采用相应路径理论时另证。
等到赢钱再走，不一定违反每一步的公平。真正危险的，是把有限期限的账本直接带到一个没有控制的终点：有时等待的平均长度无限，有时下注额把罕见损失放大，有时停止后的本钱缺少共同的可积控制。
停止时刻把“当时能不能决定”说清楚；一致可积性把“能不能在最后结账”说清楚。它们解决的是两个不同的问题。
而一次合法的返回，还留下了另一件没有保证的事。玩家重新回到同一个位置时，未来会不会仍记着此前怎样走到这里？若当前位置足以概括整段过去，一次停止便有可能成为一次真正的新开始。
本章的两种翻倍游戏、有限增量账本与反例是现代教学重建，不声称为某位历史作者原书中的同一表述。关于公平赌博进入现代鞅理论的背景，可参看第十五章已经列出的 [Doob本人访谈](https://chance.dartmouth.edu/Doob/conversation.html)。本章完整主证限于离散时间抽样；连续时间一节仅证明明示的首次命中可测性，没有预用Doob–Meyer或一般正则化。

paragraphs.signature: A player writes down a rule before the game begins: leave the table as soon as the net gain reaches one unit.

The player asks neither for a biased coin nor for knowledge of the next toss. Only the accounting time changes. If play may continue forever, the first winning moment seems bound to arrive; counting the capital then no longer looks like an experiment with mean gain zero.

In Chapter 15, fairness at each step already constrained oscillations of the path. But this player's endpoint is chosen by the path itself. We must prove anew whether a conditional average at fixed times survives that choice.
First fix a discrete-time filtration MATHINLINE"(\\mathcal F_n)_{n\\ge0}". A random variable MATHINLINE"T" with values in MATHINLINE"\\mathbb N_0\\cup\\{\\infty\\}" is a stopping time if
MATHBLOCK"\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n\\qquad(n\\ge0)."

This does not require the player to know the departure time at time zero. At time MATHINLINE"n", the player must know whether departure has already occurred. Equivalently, MATHINLINE"\\{T=n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n": take consecutive differences in one direction and finite unions in the other. Consequently MATHINLINE"\\{T\\ge k\\}\\in\\mathcal F_{k-1}". This last event will supply the indicator of a legitimate bet.

For simple symmetric random walk MATHINLINE"S_n", the first visit to 1 is a stopping time: whether 1 has been visited so far uses only steps already taken. The last visit to 0 before a fixed horizon MATHINLINE"N" generally is not. After leaving 0 one needs future information to decide whether that visit was the last. For example, with MATHINLINE"N=2", the last zero MATHINLINE"L" satisfies MATHINLINE"\\{L=0\\}=\\{S_2\\ne0\\}", an event outside the trivial MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_0".
The distinction between a random time and a stopping time concerns information, rather than whether the time is random.
For a possibly infinite stopping time define
MATHBLOCK"\\mathcal F_T=\\{A\\in\\mathcal F:\\ A\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n\\text{ for every }n\\}."

The ambient MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F" matters: the condition imposes no restriction on information on MATHINLINE"\\{T=\\infty\\}". An equivalent condition on finite slices is MATHINLINE"A\\cap\\{T=n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n". Complements and countable unions verify directly that this is a sigma-field, and MATHINLINE"T" is measurable for it.
If MATHINLINE"S\\le T", then MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_S\\subseteq\\mathcal F_T", since
MATHBLOCK"A\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}=(A\\cap\\{S\\le n\\})\\cap\\{T\\le n\\}\\in\\mathcal F_n."

If MATHINLINE"X_n" is adapted, assign the deterministic value 0 on MATHINLINE"T=\\infty" for now. Then MATHINLINE"X_T" is MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_T"-measurable: on MATHINLINE"\\{T\\le n\\}" it is a finite pasting of the variables MATHINLINE"X_k\\mathbf1_{\\{T=k\\}}". This convention does not assert that 0 is a limit at infinity. A terminal limit will be used only after its existence has been proved.

The minimum and maximum of stopping times are stopping times. If MATHINLINE"S\\le T", one also checks that MATHINLINE"A\\in\\mathcal F_S" implies MATHINLINE"A\\cap\\{S<k\\le T\\}\\in\\mathcal F_{k-1}". That is exactly the information needed for an account opened at MATHINLINE"S" and closed at MATHINLINE"T".

Put MATHINLINE"X^T_n=X_{n\\wedge T}". This is adapted by splitting into MATHINLINE"T=0,\\ldots,n-1" and MATHINLINE"T\\ge n". Finite pasting also preserves integrability. The crucial pathwise identity is

Chapter 4's particle does not appear only at integer times. The discrete theorem cannot simply stand in for continuous-time sampling, but a precise measurability fact can already be proved.
Let MATHINLINE"X_t" be a continuous adapted process in a metric space and MATHINLINE"C" closed. For fixed MATHINLINE"t", continuity and compactness of the time interval give

极限便不变。有限不可约时任何不变概率每项都为正：某项为正，沿正概率路径把正性传播到所有状态。若 MATHINLINE"\\pi,\\rho" 都不变，令 MATHINLINE"r_i=\\pi_i/\\rho_i"。由反向矩阵 MATHINLINE"\\widehat p_{ij}=\\rho_jp_{ji}/\\rho_i"，有 MATHINLINE"r_i=\\sum_j\\widehat p_{ij}r_j"。在取得最大值的状态，所有正权邻居都必须同为最大值；不可约性将它传播到全类。故比值为常数，总质量为1使常数为1。这证明唯一性。
有限性不能直接删掉。在整数直线的对称游走中，不变向量满足 MATHINLINE"2\\pi_j=\\pi_{j-1}+\\pi_{j+1}"，所以相邻差为常数。对全部整数非负只能是常数列，非零常数又不可求和。因此没有不变概率，尽管每一步的转移规则完全齐次。
两状态链每一步必换到另一状态。唯一不变分布为 MATHINLINE"(1/2,1/2)"，但从一个确定状态出发，分布永远在两个点质量间交替。
可约性还会破坏唯一性：两个互不沟通的吸收点，任何两点概率混合都不变。上述有限不可约证明并没有自动证明所有无限链的平稳极限，也没有消除周期。返回次数与平均返回时间的理论，会进一步告诉我们什么时候存在可归一化的长期占用预算。
若 MATHINLINE"\\pi_i>0"，平稳链的反向一步核必须为
MATHBLOCK"\\widehat p_{ij}=\\frac{\\pi_jp_{ji}}{\\pi_i}."
不变性保证每行和为1，且 MATHINLINE"\\pi\\widehat P=\\pi"。把相邻两时刻的联合概率 MATHINLINE"\\pi_ip_{ij}" 倒放就得到这个式子；更长的路径由乘积中的 MATHINLINE"\\pi" 比值逐项消去验证。若某状态的平稳质量为0，只在正质量支撑上使用该公式；零质量状态的反向行可以另行任取，不会改变平稳路径律。
若 MATHINLINE"\\pi_ip_{ij}=\\pi_jp_{ji}" 对所有两状态成立，称为详细平衡。求和便得到不变性；连乘则得到每条有限平稳路径与其反向路径等概率，这称为可逆性。反过来，可逆性在长度1的路径上便给出详细平衡，因此两者在这里等价。
不变性弱于可逆性。三个状态沿一个有向环确定旋转，均匀分布不变，但正向边概率非零、反向边概率为零，详细平衡失败。平稳不表示没有时间方向。
一个状态之所以有用，不是因为它小，而是因为它保留了预测未来所需的信息。核把这个要求写成可测的概率规则，顺序扩张使规则拥有真正的无限记录，停止时刻分片则说明合法停下以后仍可从当前位置继续。
然而，未来的规则重新相同，并不保证未来的结局相同。路径可以在同一类状态间反复交替，也可以不断走向远处；一个形式上能走回来的位置，未必真的会再被看见。我们需要把“可以到达”与“最终会回来”分开计算。
本章的比特反例、循环链与核账本采用现代重建。Markov性质不是任何过程天然具有的无记忆口号，离散强Markov也不是任意连续时间过程的默认性质。[Ionescu–Tulcea顺序构造补证](../foundations/t-sequential.md)完整承担这里的一般可测空间存在性；第十章的标准Borel随机化仍保持其原有范围，不被倒记为一般空间证明。
顺序实验的原始文献入口为Ionescu–Tulcea的1949年论文[Mesures dans les espaces produits](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~y328yu/classics/IonescuTulcea49.pdf)。这里采用前缀成功概率的现代重建，区分顺序核所提供的额外相容结构与任意一般空间有限维分布的扩张问题。
At a lattice site, the chances of moving left or right do not depend on how many streets were traversed before arrival. Standing at the same place again seems to restore the same future.

Randomness alone does not guarantee this. If a coin's bias is an unknown parameter, earlier observations alter our prediction of the next toss; current position need not record every useful piece of information. For a return to be a genuine restart, we must identify what the present summarizes and what remains hidden in the past.

Let an adapted process MATHINLINE"X_n" take values in a measurable space MATHINLINE"(E,\\mathcal E)". Given a probability kernel MATHINLINE"P(x,dy)", the homogeneous Markov property relative to MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_n" means, for every bounded measurable MATHINLINE"f",
MATHBLOCK"E[f(X_{n+1})\\mid\\mathcal F_n]=Pf(X_n),\\qquad Pf(x)=\\int f(y)P(x,dy)."

Homogeneity means the same kernel applies at every time; a time-inhomogeneous system may use MATHINLINE"P_n". A kernel has two separate requirements: each MATHINLINE"x" specifies a probability measure, and each event's probability varies measurably with MATHINLINE"x". Both are needed for the right side to be a legitimate random prediction.

The property refers to a specified filtration. Enlarging it to reveal future outcomes can destroy the Markov property. Validity for the natural filtration does not imply validity for every larger filtration.

Take independent fair bits MATHINLINE"U,V" and set MATHINLINE"X_0=U,X_1=V,X_2=U". Each has the same fair marginal, and adjacent pairs are independent. Yet MATHINLINE"X_0,X_1" determine MATHINLINE"X_2", whereas given only MATHINLINE"X_1" its two possibilities still have equal probability.

Thus identical distributions at each time are far from saying the past supplies no further prediction. Even adjacent joint laws may be insufficient. Enlarging the state can preserve discarded memory: recording the relevant history as part of the state often produces a larger Markov system. This is a modeling choice, not a theorem that arbitrary projections preserve the Markov property.

Chapter 15's conditional independence gives precise language. Since MATHINLINE"\\sigma(X_n)\\subseteq\\mathcal F_n", the defining equality says that MATHINLINE"\\sigma(X_{n+1})" and MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_n" are conditionally independent given MATHINLINE"\\sigma(X_n)". Conversely, that conditional independence recovers the Markov equality provided the specified kernel really is a conditional law of the next state given MATHINLINE"X_n". On general measurable spaces, existence of conditional expectations does not itself supply such a kernel; here the kernel is data or is explicitly constructed.
Define MATHINLINE"P^0(x,A)=\\mathbf1_A(x)", and put
MATHBLOCK"P^{n+1}(x,A)=\\int P^n(y,A)P(x,dy)."

Measurability of kernel integrals was proved in Chapter 10. The tower property and induction yield MATHINLINE"E[f(X_{n+r})\\mid\\mathcal F_n]=P^rf(X_n)". Associativity of iterated integration then gives the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation
MATHBLOCK"P^{r+s}(x,A)=\\int P^s(y,A)P^r(x,dy)."

Prove associativity for nonnegative functions with Tonelli, then split bounded signed functions into positive and negative parts. This supplies the justification for extending matrix multiplication to general spaces.

Successive conditional averaging also treats finite future blocks. For bounded measurable MATHINLINE"H" of the next MATHINLINE"r" states, let MATHINLINE"Q_rH(x)" be its MATHINLINE"r"-fold kernel integral starting from MATHINLINE"x". Then
MATHBLOCK"E[H(X_{n+1},\\ldots,X_{n+r})\\mid\\mathcal F_n]=Q_rH(X_n)."

First verify products of indicators, then finite linear combinations, then a functional monotone class. The present therefore summarizes every finite future experiment, rather than only its next step.
Given initial probability MATHINLINE"\\nu" and kernel MATHINLINE"P", finite paths should have law
MATHBLOCK"\\nu(dx_0)P(x_0,dx_1)\\cdots P(x_{n-1},dx_n)."

These are still only finite experiments. Chapter 10 constructed sequential experiments on standard Borel spaces through randomization; arbitrary measurable spaces cannot silently inherit that encoding. General finite kernel products are available from [10.9](10-densities-and-kernels.md#section-10-9), but they do not yet give a countably infinite construction. Here the input must be a probability kernel at every prefix, not merely a collection of almost-everywhere conditional-expectation versions.

[T-SEQUENTIAL](../foundations/t-sequential.md#t-sequential-extension) proves the countable construction on general measurable spaces. It defines finite integrals on the cylinder algebra and proves continuity at an empty decreasing intersection. The mechanism is concrete: if the probabilities of decreasing cylinders stay positive, conditional future success probabilities allow coordinates to be chosen successively, producing a record in every cylinder, contradicting the empty intersection. The choices need not be measurable functions of their prefixes, so no unjustified measurable-selection theorem is needed.

After extension, the kernel-integral identities on all prefix events verify Markov conditional averaging itself. Both existence and the property have been established, using only countable sequential experiments rather than future continuous-process theory or an uncountable extension.

Let MATHINLINE"T" be an almost surely finite stopping time. Split MATHINLINE"A\\in\\mathcal F_T" according to MATHINLINE"T=n"; each slice belongs to MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_n". The fixed-time future formula gives
MATHBLOCK"E[\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T=n\\}}H(X_{T+1},\\ldots,X_{T+r})]\n=E[\\mathbf1_{A\\cap\\{T=n\\}}Q_rH(X_T)]."
Boundedness permits summation over every MATHINLINE"n", yielding
MATHBLOCK"E[H(X_{T+1},\\ldots,X_{T+r})\\mid\\mathcal F_T]=Q_rH(X_T)."

This is the discrete strong Markov property. If MATHINLINE"T" can be infinite, understand it only on MATHINLINE"T<\\infty": sum on MATHINLINE"A\\cap\\{T<\\infty\\}", without inventing steps after MATHINLINE"X_\\infty". For the entire countable future, extend from cylinders by a monotone class.

This proof does not infer independence from optional sampling. It uses slices of the stopped sigma-field and the original Markov kernel. Continuous time has no such countable partition covering every real stopping value; general strong Markov properties there need additional regular structure.

Now take a finite or countable state space with its discrete sigma-field, and write MATHINLINE"p_{ij}" for the transition matrix. Write MATHINLINE"i\\to j" if MATHINLINE"p^{(n)}_{ij}>0" for some MATHINLINE"n\\ge0". This relation is reflexive and transitive; transitivity follows from one positive product in Chapman–Kolmogorov. Mutual accessibility MATHINLINE"i\\leftrightarrow j" therefore partitions the space into communication classes.

A class with no outward transitions is closed. A finite chain has at least one closed class: collapse communication classes to a finite directed acyclic graph and follow outward edges until a class with no outward edge is reached. An infinite chain can instead keep moving into new states without a closed finite region.

Accessibility asserts existence of a positive-probability route, not inevitable arrival along every record. Communication is not recurrence either: an infinite system with a possible route back from every state may still avoid its starting state forever with positive probability.
For a state MATHINLINE"i" with a possible positive-time return, define
MATHBLOCK"d(i)=\\gcd\\{n\\ge1:p^{(n)}_{ii}>0\\}."

The period is the same within a communication class. Choose positive-probability paths MATHINLINE"i\\to j" and MATHINLINE"j\\to i", of lengths MATHINLINE"a,b". If MATHINLINE"j" returns in MATHINLINE"n" steps, then MATHINLINE"i" returns in both MATHINLINE"a+n+b" and MATHINLINE"a+b" steps, so MATHINLINE"d(i)" divides MATHINLINE"n". Interchange the states to obtain equality of periods.

All paths from a fixed base to another state have the same length modulo MATHINLINE"d": append a common return path to two such paths, and their length difference is divisible by MATHINLINE"d". An irreducible class therefore divides into cyclic residue classes. Nearest-neighbor line walk returns only at even times and has period 2; adding a positive chance of staying put reduces the period to 1.

Period does not decide whether a return occurs, but it rules out certain return times altogether. It also explains why existence of an invariant probability does not alone imply convergence of the step-by-step distributions.

A probability vector MATHINLINE"\\pi" is invariant if MATHINLINE"\\pi P=\\pi". Starting with MATHINLINE"\\pi" gives the same finite-dimensional distributions after a time shift: write the path product and sum out the earliest coordinate. Individual paths may continue jumping indefinitely.

Every finite chain has an invariant distribution. For any initial law MATHINLINE"\\nu", take Cesàro averages MATHINLINE"\\mu_N=N^{-1}\\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\\nu P^k". In a finite-dimensional probability simplex one may extract a coordinatewise convergent subsequence, while
MATHBLOCK"\\mu_NP-\\mu_N=(\\nu P^N-\\nu)/N\\longrightarrow0."

The limit is invariant. In a finite irreducible chain every coordinate of any invariant probability is positive: positivity propagates along positive-probability paths. If MATHINLINE"\\pi,\\rho" are invariant, put MATHINLINE"r_i=\\pi_i/\\rho_i". The reversed matrix MATHINLINE"\\widehat p_{ij}=\\rho_jp_{ji}/\\rho_i" gives MATHINLINE"r_i=\\sum_j\\widehat p_{ij}r_j". At a state maximizing the ratio, all neighbors with positive weights must also maximize it. Irreducibility propagates that maximum throughout the class. The ratio is constant, and total mass one makes it 1. This proves uniqueness.

Finiteness cannot simply be removed. In symmetric walk on the integer line, invariance requires MATHINLINE"2\\pi_j=\\pi_{j-1}+\\pi_{j+1}", so neighboring differences are constant. Nonnegativity on all integers forces a constant sequence, and a nonzero constant cannot be summable. There is no invariant probability despite completely homogeneous transition rules.

A two-state chain switches states at every step. Its unique invariant distribution is MATHINLINE"(1/2,1/2)", but from a deterministic state its distributions alternate forever between two point masses.

Reducibility can also destroy uniqueness: with two isolated absorbing states, every mixture of their point masses is invariant. The finite irreducible argument proved neither stationary limits for all infinite chains nor removal of periodicity. Return counts and mean return times will explain when a long-term occupation budget can be normalized.
Where MATHINLINE"\\pi_i>0", a stationary chain's reversed one-step kernel must be
MATHBLOCK"\\widehat p_{ij}=\\frac{\\pi_jp_{ji}}{\\pi_i}."

Invariance makes its row sums one, and MATHINLINE"\\pi\\widehat P=\\pi". Reversing the two-time joint mass MATHINLINE"\\pi_ip_{ij}" gives the formula; for longer paths, successive factors involving MATHINLINE"\\pi" cancel in the product. If a state has stationary mass zero, use the formula only on the positive-mass support. Reversed rows at zero-mass states may be assigned separately without changing the stationary path law.

The equalities MATHINLINE"\\pi_ip_{ij}=\\pi_jp_{ji}" for all pairs are detailed balance. Summation proves invariance; multiplication proves that every finite stationary path and its reversal have equal probabilities, called reversibility. Conversely, reversibility on one-step paths gives detailed balance, so these properties are equivalent here.

Invariance is weaker than reversibility. Deterministic rotation around a directed three-state cycle preserves the uniform law, but forward edges have positive probability and reversed edges have probability zero. Detailed balance fails. Stationarity need not erase the direction of time.

A state is useful because it retains what is needed to predict the future, rather than merely because it is small. A kernel turns that requirement into a measurable probability rule; sequential extension supplies actual infinite records; stopping-time slices show that after a legitimate stop the process can continue from its present state.

The same future rule does not guarantee the same future outcome. Paths may keep alternating within a class or move ever farther away. A position accessible by some possible route need never be seen again. We must distinguish being able to return from actually returning.

The bit counterexample, cyclic chains and kernel accounts are modern reconstructions. The Markov property is not automatic memorylessness of every random process, and the discrete strong Markov result is not a default assertion for arbitrary continuous-time processes. The [Ionescu–Tulcea construction supplement](../foundations/t-sequential.md) supplies the complete general-measurable-space existence proof used here. Chapter 10's standard Borel randomization retains its original scope and is not retrospectively counted as a proof for general spaces.

An original source for sequential experiments is Ionescu–Tulcea's 1949 paper [Mesures dans les espaces produits](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~y328yu/classics/IonescuTulcea49.pdf). The prefix-success-probability argument here is a modern reconstruction. It distinguishes the additional compatible structure supplied by sequential kernels from extension of arbitrary finite-dimensional laws on general spaces.
向左一步，向右一步，平均起来没有离开的方向。然而，在三维格点中，一个每一步都不偏向任何方向的行者，仍有正概率从此再也不回到出发点。
这不是第四章缩放图像所能回答的问题。那里把很多微小步子压进有限的时间窗口；这里固定每一步的大小，让时间无限延长。我们要数的不是最后站在哪里，而是同一个地方究竟还会被看见多少次。
对可数状态Markov链，从 MATHINLINE"i" 出发，定义首次正时间返回
MATHBLOCK"T_i=\\inf\\{n\\ge1:X_n=i\\},\\qquad f_i=P_i(T_i<\\infty)."
若 MATHINLINE"f_i=1"，称 MATHINLINE"i" 常返；若 MATHINLINE"f_i<1"，称其暂留，也称暂态。这里返回规则从1开始，否则初始位置会使返回概率恒为1而抹去全部问题。
记 MATHINLINE"N_i=\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=i\\}}"，包括初始访问。第十七章的离散强Markov性质使每次返回后的下一次返回概率仍为 MATHINLINE"f_i"。对逐次返回时刻归纳得到
MATHBLOCK"P_i(N_i\\ge k)=f_i^{k-1},\\qquad\nE_iN_i=\\sum_{k\\ge1}f_i^{k-1}."
于是常返时访问无穷次几乎必然；暂留时访问有限次几乎必然，且平均访问次数为 MATHINLINE"1/(1-f_i)"。无限平均在一般随机变量上未必推出几乎必然无限，但这里几何重启的结构使它成为等价。
定义Green核
MATHBLOCK"G(i,j)=\\sum_{n=0}^\\infty p^{(n)}_{ij}=E_i\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=j\\}}."
最后的等式由非负积分的Tonelli得到。因此
MATHBLOCK"G(i,i)=\\infty\\ \\Longleftrightarrow\\ f_i=1,\\qquad\nG(i,i)=\\frac1{1-f_i}\\quad(f_i<1)."
若 MATHINLINE"H_j" 是包括时刻0的首次命中 MATHINLINE"j"，强Markov还给出 MATHINLINE"G(i,j)=P_i(H_j<\\infty)G(j,j)"，作为非负扩展积分理解；概率为0时右边按0解释，不写未定义的 MATHINLINE"0\\cdot\\infty"。先在命中事件分片，再用单调收敛累计所有后续访问，即可证明这一式。
所以一系列固定时刻的概率，可以合起来回答一条无限路径的问题。这与仅知道某个固定时刻的边缘不同：我们同时利用了返回后的再生关系。
令 MATHINLINE"u_n=P_i(X_n=i)"，MATHINLINE"a_k=P_i(T_i=k)"。对首次返回时间分片，得到
MATHBLOCK"u_0=1,\\qquad u_n=\\sum_{k=1}^na_ku_{n-k}\\quad(n\\ge1)."
在 MATHINLINE"0\\le z<1" 上所有级数绝对收敛，故母函数满足 MATHINLINE"U(z)=1+A(z)U(z)"，即 MATHINLINE"U(z)=1/(1-A(z))"。令 MATHINLINE"z\\uparrow1" 就恢复Green判别。首次返回分布可以有缺失质量：总和小于1，恰好表示某些路径根本没有下一周期。
这个更新方程将成为下一章的起点。此刻我们先用另一种读数计算 MATHINLINE"u_n"，看看空间维度怎样改变级数。
考虑 MATHINLINE"\\mathbb Z^d" 上的简单对称最近邻游走，每一步从 MATHINLINE"2d" 个方向等概率选择，独立重复。单步特征函数为
MATHBLOCK"\\phi(\\theta)=\\frac1d\\sum_{j=1}^d\\cos\\theta_j,\n\\qquad\\theta\\in[-\\pi,\\pi]^d."
对任何整数向量 MATHINLINE"k"，各坐标指数积分相乘给出
MATHBLOCK"(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}e^{i\\theta\\cdot k}\\,d\\theta\n=\\mathbf1_{\\{k=0\\}}."
先对随机位置取期望再用有界Fubini，便得到 MATHINLINE"u_n=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int\\phi(\\theta)^n\\,d\\theta"。这里无需借用一般局部中心极限定理，也不把弱极限当作单点概率近似。
直接把可能有负号的 MATHINLINE"\\phi^n" 无限求和，不能随意交换积分。先取 MATHINLINE"0<r<1"，其绝对和由 MATHINLINE"1/(1-r)" 控制，于是
MATHBLOCK"G_r(0,0)=\\sum_{n\\ge0}r^nu_n\n=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}\\frac{d\\theta}{1-r\\phi(\\theta)}."
左边随 MATHINLINE"r\\uparrow1" 单调趋于Green和。积分右边在 MATHINLINE"\\phi\\ge0" 区域用单调收敛，在 MATHINLINE"\\phi<0" 区域被1控制而用DCT。因此作为允许无穷的等式，
MATHBLOCK"G(0,0)=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}\\frac{d\\theta}{1-\\phi(\\theta)}."
折扣没有改变最终的问题，却使每一步极限交换都有正当依据。我们现在只需判断一个确定积分是否有限。
在这块周期区域内，MATHINLINE"\\phi=1" 只可能发生在所有坐标为0之处。由 MATHINLINE"1-\\cos t" 与 MATHINLINE"t^2" 在0附近的双边比较，存在正数 MATHINLINE"c,C,\\delta"，使
MATHBLOCK"c|\\theta|^2\\le1-\\phi(\\theta)\\le C|\\theta|^2\n\\qquad(|\\theta|<\\delta)."

离开原点小球，连续函数 MATHINLINE"1-\\phi" 有严格正的下界。小球内的可积性则与 MATHINLINE"\\int_0^\\delta \\rho^{d-3}\\,d\\rho" 相同；也可以不用球坐标，分成尺度 MATHINLINE"2^{-k}" 的环带，其体积与 MATHINLINE"2^{-kd}" 比较，函数大小与 MATHINLINE"2^{2k}" 比较，得到同一几何级数。
因此一维、二维积分发散，三维及更高维积分有限。结合18.2，我们完整得到Pólya判别：
MATHBLOCK"P_0(T_0<\\infty)=1\\quad(d=1,2),\\qquad\nP_0(T_0<\\infty)<1\\quad(d\\ge3)."
每个坐标没有平均漂移，仍不足以决定是否回来。更多维度提供了更多可逃离的方向；数学上，它表现为原点附近同一个二阶奇性，要由多少维体积来承担。
最近邻游走每走一步都改变坐标和的奇偶性，因此奇数时刻不可能返回。第十三章已经说明，单点Gaussian近似必须把允许格点与跨度计入。
在这里，MATHINLINE"\\phi=-1" 的角点不使 MATHINLINE"1-\\phi" 产生奇性，所以Green判别只由 MATHINLINE"\\phi=1" 附近控制。这不表示偶数步概率可以忽略另一个角点：若直接估计 MATHINLINE"u_{2n}"，正负两处峰都会参与。累计访问判别与逐时局部近似是两件不同的事。
加入独立概率 MATHINLINE"h\\in(0,1)" 的原地等待后，新读数为 MATHINLINE"h+(1-h)\\phi"，故新Green积分恰为原来的 MATHINLINE"1/(1-h)" 倍。周期变为1，常返或暂留分类却不变。等待改变了时钟，没有增加空间上的逃离机会。
在直线游走中若 MATHINLINE"p>q"，从1命中0的概率为 MATHINLINE"q/p"：在 MATHINLINE"[0,a]" 使用第十六章的赌博破产公式，再令 MATHINLINE"a\\to\\infty" 即得。有限时间命中0的路径必有有限最大值，所以这些有限区间事件的并正是最终命中事件。
从−1命中0的概率为1。可以同样扩大左边界，也可由第十二章强大数律看出位置最终向右趋于无穷，最近邻路径必先经过0。于是首次一步分片给出
MATHBLOCK"f_0=p(q/p)+q=2q<1."
当 MATHINLINE"p<q" 时对称地得到 MATHINLINE"f_0=2p"。所以一维常返结论对无偏性很敏感；不能只凭空间是一条线，就断言一切随机运动都会回来。
若 MATHINLINE"i" 常返，并且 MATHINLINE"i\\to j"，每次返回 MATHINLINE"i" 都有同一个正概率沿固定有限路径到达 MATHINLINE"j"。按不重叠的尝试分块，失败概率至多几何下降，因此从 MATHINLINE"i" 最终命中 MATHINLINE"j" 的概率为1。

从 MATHINLINE"j" 也必须以概率1命中 MATHINLINE"i"。否则取一条从 MATHINLINE"i" 首次抵达 MATHINLINE"j" 而中间不再经过 MATHINLINE"i" 的正概率路径，再接上从 MATHINLINE"j" 避开 MATHINLINE"i" 的正概率事件，便使 MATHINLINE"i" 有正概率不返回，矛盾。重复使用强Markov，便知 MATHINLINE"j" 也被无限访问。因此与常返状态沟通的所有状态常返；常返沟通类必闭。
暂留链从任意初始状态访问指定暂留状态的次数也几乎必然有限：若命中，就从首次命中以后使用几何访问次数；若不命中，次数为0。对可数多个状态取共同零集，路径最终离开每一个固定有限集合。这是暂留的一种精确“消失”，不是位置必有一个方向性的极限。
常返状态进一步按 MATHINLINE"E_iT_i<\\infty" 或 MATHINLINE"E_iT_i=\\infty" 分成正常返与零常返。若从 MATHINLINE"i" 出发的一个完整返回周期中，状态 MATHINLINE"j" 的平均访问次数为
MATHBLOCK"\\nu_j=E_i\\sum_{n=0}^{T_i-1}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=j\\}},"
则 MATHINLINE"\\nu_i=1"，且 MATHINLINE"\\nu P=\\nu"。证明是把一步转移后的计数改成时刻1至 MATHINLINE"T_i" 的计数：起点与终点都为 MATHINLINE"i"，两端恰好抵消。所有交换先按非负积分理解。

不可约常返时每项 MATHINLINE"\\nu_j" 有限。因为从 MATHINLINE"j" 有一条在返回 MATHINLINE"j" 之前命中 MATHINLINE"i" 的正概率路径，故到达 MATHINLINE"j" 后、命中 MATHINLINE"i" 前的访问次数被一个有限均值的几何次数控制。若 MATHINLINE"E_iT_i<\\infty"，总质量 MATHINLINE"\\sum_j\\nu_j=E_iT_i"，于是可归一化成不变概率。
这项构造说明，不变概率不是凭空求出的矩阵特征向量。它可以是一个真实返回周期的占用预算，除以这个周期的平均长度。

反过来，设不可约可数链有不变概率 MATHINLINE"\\pi"。先选一个正质量状态，再沿正概率路径用不变方程传播，得每项 MATHINLINE"\\pi_i>0"。在平稳初始律下，事件“时刻 MATHINLINE"n" 在 MATHINLINE"i"，以后再也不来”对不同 MATHINLINE"n" 互斥；有限块的平稳性再取递减极限，使每个事件的概率都为 MATHINLINE"\\pi_i(1-f_i)"。无限相加不超过1，故 MATHINLINE"f_i=1"，且这对每个状态成立。这里没有借用一般遍历定理。

还要让余项真正消失。由18.9，从任意状态 MATHINLINE"k" 都几乎必然命中 MATHINLINE"i"：一条离开 MATHINLINE"k" 后不再经过它的正概率命中路径，可以在逐次返回 MATHINLINE"k" 时重新尝试，连续失败概率受几何尾控制。记 MATHINLINE"H_i=\\inf\\{n\\ge0:X_n=i\\}"、MATHINLINE"D=E\\setminus\\{i\\}"，令 MATHINLINE"K=(p_{k\\ell})_{k,\\ell\\in D}" 为杀死于 MATHINLINE"i" 的次随机矩阵，MATHINLINE"b=(p_{ij})_{j\\in D}"。不变方程在 MATHINLINE"D" 上给出
MATHBLOCK"\\pi_D=\\pi_i b+\\pi_DK\n=\\pi_i\\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}bK^r+\\pi_DK^N."
对 MATHINLINE"j\\in D"，MATHINLINE"\\sum_{r\\ge0}(bK^r)_j=\\nu_j"：这些恰是从 MATHINLINE"i" 出发、第一次返回以前各时刻的访问概率。余项的总质量则为
MATHBLOCK"\\sum_{j\\in D}(\\pi_DK^N)_j\n=\\sum_{k\\in D}\\pi_kP_k(H_i>N)\\longrightarrow0."
每个命中尾概率趋0，并由可求和的 MATHINLINE"\\pi_k" 控制，故这里是有依据的控制收敛；前一项由非负单调收敛趋于 MATHINLINE"\\pi_i\\nu_j"。加上 MATHINLINE"\\nu_i=1"，再对全部状态求和，便得到
MATHBLOCK"\\pi_j=\\pi_i\\nu_j,\\qquad E_iT_i=1/\\pi_i."
周期预算于是唯一地决定不变概率。直线对称游走常返，却由第十七章知道没有不变概率，所以必为零常返。有限不可约链有不变概率，因此每个状态正常返；它仍可能因周期而不逐步收敛。
对一般实值独立增量游走 MATHINLINE"S_n"，首次严格超过初值的时刻 MATHINLINE"L" 与高度 MATHINLINE"H=S_L"，可以组成一个有缺失质量的联合分布：有些路径可能永不创造新高。每次新高以后，独立增量与停止分片使下一次新高的时间差、高度差具有同一联合规律。

若 MATHINLINE"q(z,\\theta)=E[z^Le^{i\\theta H};L<\\infty]"，其中 MATHINLINE"0\\le z<1"，则所有严格上升纪录的联合变换之和为 MATHINLINE"\\sum_{k\\ge0}q(z,\\theta)^k=1/(1-q(z,\\theta))"。因为 MATHINLINE"|q(z,\\theta)|\\le z<1"，交换与求和有绝对控制。这是离散梯级更新结构的实质证明。
它还不是把整个游走分成上升、下降两部分的完整Wiener–Hopf因子分解；严格与弱梯级的边界约定及完整乘积分解仍须另外证明。我们保留这个准确边界，不用一个名称宣告已经建立全部离散或Lévy因子分解。
没有漂移的步子，在二维与三维之间跨过了一条真正的边界。区别并不来自一次跳跃，而来自无穷次可能返回所需要的总预算。Green和把这个预算写出来，Fourier积分则把它化成原点附近体积与奇性的竞争。
一旦返回发生，未来又从同一个状态出发。沿着一条记录，时间便被切成一个个周期。有的周期永远等不到，有的总会结束却没有有限均值。若要把这些重新开始合起来计算长期等待，下一步就不再只是判断回来与否，而是研究周期怎样填满时间。

Pólya的论文《Über eine Aufgabe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung betreffend die Irrfahrt im Straßennetz》刊于1921年的《Mathematische Annalen》84卷，149–160页。本章的折扣Fourier证明使用已经建立的特征函数和积分工具，是现代重建，不声称复制原论文证明。原文与出版元数据见 [Pólya论文](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01458701)。本章完整判别的是简单对称最近邻格点游走；任意步长、相关步子或一般群上的常返性不能由维度口号代替证明。

A step left and a step right leave no preferred direction on average. Yet on a three-dimensional lattice, a walker with no directional preference at any step has positive probability of never revisiting its starting point.

Chapter 4's scaling picture does not answer this question. There, many tiny steps were compressed into a finite time window. Here step size stays fixed while time extends indefinitely. We count not the final position, but how often the same place will be seen again.
For a countable-state Markov chain started at MATHINLINE"i", define the first positive-time return
MATHBLOCK"T_i=\\inf\\{n\\ge1:X_n=i\\},\\qquad f_i=P_i(T_i<\\infty)."

The state MATHINLINE"i" is recurrent if MATHINLINE"f_i=1", and transient if MATHINLINE"f_i<1". Starting the return rule at 1 matters: otherwise the initial visit would make the probability identically one and erase the question.

Let MATHINLINE"N_i=\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=i\\}}", counting the initial visit. The discrete strong Markov property of Chapter 17 makes the probability of another return after each return equal to MATHINLINE"f_i". Induction at successive returns gives
MATHBLOCK"P_i(N_i\\ge k)=f_i^{k-1},\\qquad\nE_iN_i=\\sum_{k\\ge1}f_i^{k-1}."

A recurrent state is therefore visited infinitely often almost surely. A transient state has finitely many visits almost surely, with mean MATHINLINE"1/(1-f_i)". For a general random variable infinite mean need not imply an almost surely infinite value; the geometric restart structure makes them equivalent here.
Define the Green kernel
MATHBLOCK"G(i,j)=\\sum_{n=0}^\\infty p^{(n)}_{ij}=E_i\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=j\\}}."
Tonelli for nonnegative integrals gives the last equality. Consequently
MATHBLOCK"G(i,i)=\\infty\\ \\Longleftrightarrow\\ f_i=1,\\qquad\nG(i,i)=\\frac1{1-f_i}\\quad(f_i<1)."

If MATHINLINE"H_j" is the first hit of MATHINLINE"j", including time zero, strong Markov also gives MATHINLINE"G(i,j)=P_i(H_j<\\infty)G(j,j)" as a nonnegative extended integral. When the probability is zero, interpret the right side as zero, not an undefined MATHINLINE"0\\cdot\\infty". Split over the hitting event and then accumulate future visits by monotone convergence to prove the identity.
Thus probabilities at fixed times can together answer a question about an infinite path. We use more than one marginal: the renewal relation after returns supplies the extra structure.
Put MATHINLINE"u_n=P_i(X_n=i)" and MATHINLINE"a_k=P_i(T_i=k)". Splitting according to first return gives
MATHBLOCK"u_0=1,\\qquad u_n=\\sum_{k=1}^na_ku_{n-k}\\quad(n\\ge1)."

For MATHINLINE"0\\le z<1" the series converge absolutely. Their generating functions satisfy MATHINLINE"U(z)=1+A(z)U(z)", hence MATHINLINE"U(z)=1/(1-A(z))". Letting MATHINLINE"z\\uparrow1" recovers the Green criterion. The first-return law may be defective: total mass below one records paths with no next cycle.
This renewal equation will begin the next chapter. For now, another readout of MATHINLINE"u_n" will show how dimension changes the series.
Consider simple symmetric nearest-neighbor walk on MATHINLINE"\\mathbb Z^d". Each independent step chooses uniformly among MATHINLINE"2d" directions. Its characteristic function is
MATHBLOCK"\\phi(\\theta)=\\frac1d\\sum_{j=1}^d\\cos\\theta_j,\n\\qquad\\theta\\in[-\\pi,\\pi]^d."
For every integer vector MATHINLINE"k", multiplying the coordinate exponential integrals yields
MATHBLOCK"(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}e^{i\\theta\\cdot k}\\,d\\theta\n=\\mathbf1_{\\{k=0\\}}."

Take expectation at the random position and use bounded Fubini to obtain MATHINLINE"u_n=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int\\phi(\\theta)^n\\,d\\theta". No general local CLT is required, and weak convergence has not been substituted for a point-probability estimate.
The powers MATHINLINE"\\phi^n" may have either sign, so summing them under an integral needs justification. First take MATHINLINE"0<r<1". The absolute sum is bounded by MATHINLINE"1/(1-r)", giving
MATHBLOCK"G_r(0,0)=\\sum_{n\\ge0}r^nu_n\n=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}\\frac{d\\theta}{1-r\\phi(\\theta)}."

The left side increases to the Green sum as MATHINLINE"r\\uparrow1". On the region MATHINLINE"\\phi\\ge0" use monotone convergence; on MATHINLINE"\\phi<0" the integrand is bounded by 1, so use DCT. As an equality allowing infinity,
MATHBLOCK"G(0,0)=(2\\pi)^{-d}\\int_{[-\\pi,\\pi]^d}\\frac{d\\theta}{1-\\phi(\\theta)}."
Discounting leaves the eventual question unchanged while justifying every interchange. The problem is now whether a deterministic integral is finite.

In this periodic domain, MATHINLINE"\\phi=1" requires all coordinates to vanish. The two-sided comparison of MATHINLINE"1-\\cos t" with MATHINLINE"t^2" near zero gives positive MATHINLINE"c,C,\\delta" such that
MATHBLOCK"c|\\theta|^2\\le1-\\phi(\\theta)\\le C|\\theta|^2\n\\qquad(|\\theta|<\\delta)."

Away from a small ball, continuity gives a positive lower bound for MATHINLINE"1-\\phi". Inside it, integrability is equivalent to that of MATHINLINE"\\int_0^\\delta \\rho^{d-3}\\,d\\rho". Alternatively, decompose into annuli of scale MATHINLINE"2^{-k}": their volumes are comparable to MATHINLINE"2^{-kd}" and the integrand to MATHINLINE"2^{2k}", producing the same geometric-series test without polar coordinates.
The integral diverges in dimensions one and two, and is finite from dimension three onward. Combined with 18.2, this proves Pólya's criterion:
MATHBLOCK"P_0(T_0<\\infty)=1\\quad(d=1,2),\\qquad\nP_0(T_0<\\infty)<1\\quad(d\\ge3)."

Zero average drift in every coordinate does not decide return. More dimensions supply more routes of escape; analytically, the same quadratic singularity must be supported by different amounts of surrounding volume.

Each nearest-neighbor step changes the parity of the coordinate sum, so odd-time return is impossible. Chapter 13 explained why a pointwise Gaussian approximation must account for allowed lattice sites and span.

Here a corner with MATHINLINE"\\phi=-1" creates no singularity in MATHINLINE"1-\\phi", so the Green test is governed by MATHINLINE"\\phi=1". That does not license ignoring the other corner when estimating MATHINLINE"u_{2n}" itself: both positive and negative peaks contribute there. An accumulated-visit test and a fixed-time local approximation are different calculations.

Add an independent holding probability MATHINLINE"h\\in(0,1)". The new readout is MATHINLINE"h+(1-h)\\phi", so the Green integral is multiplied by MATHINLINE"1/(1-h)". Period becomes one, but recurrence or transience does not change. Holding changes the clock without adding spatial routes of escape.

For line walk with MATHINLINE"p>q", the chance of hitting 0 from 1 is MATHINLINE"q/p": apply Chapter 16's ruin formula on MATHINLINE"[0,a]" and let MATHINLINE"a\\to\\infty". A path that hits 0 at a finite time has a finite maximum before that hit, so the union of these finite-interval events is exactly eventual hitting.

From −1 the chance of hitting 0 is one. Enlarge the left barrier in the same way, or use Chapter 12's strong law to see the position eventually tending rightward to infinity, which a nearest-neighbor path cannot do without crossing 0. Splitting on the first step gives
MATHBLOCK"f_0=p(q/p)+q=2q<1."
For MATHINLINE"p<q", symmetry gives MATHINLINE"f_0=2p". One-dimensional recurrence is sensitive to lack of bias; merely living on a line does not make every random motion return.

Suppose MATHINLINE"i" is recurrent and MATHINLINE"i\\to j". After each return to MATHINLINE"i", the same positive probability is available for following a fixed finite route to MATHINLINE"j". Group attempts into nonoverlapping blocks; failure probabilities decay geometrically. Starting from MATHINLINE"i", the chain therefore eventually hits MATHINLINE"j" almost surely.

Starting from MATHINLINE"j", it must also hit MATHINLINE"i" almost surely. Otherwise choose a positive-probability route from MATHINLINE"i" to its first arrival at MATHINLINE"j", with no intervening return to MATHINLINE"i", then a positive-probability future avoiding MATHINLINE"i". This would give positive probability of no return to MATHINLINE"i", a contradiction. Iterating strong Markov shows infinitely many visits to MATHINLINE"j". Thus MATHINLINE"j" and every state communicating with a recurrent state is recurrent, and recurrent classes are closed.

From any initial state, a specified transient state is visited finitely often almost surely: upon a hit, its remaining visits have the geometric law; without a hit, their number is zero. Taking a common null set over countably many states, the path eventually leaves every fixed finite set. This is a precise sense of escape, not a claim that position has a directional limit.

A recurrent state is positive recurrent if MATHINLINE"E_iT_i<\\infty", and null recurrent if MATHINLINE"E_iT_i=\\infty". Let the mean visits to MATHINLINE"j" in one complete return cycle from MATHINLINE"i" be
MATHBLOCK"\\nu_j=E_i\\sum_{n=0}^{T_i-1}\\mathbf1_{\\{X_n=j\\}},"

Then MATHINLINE"\\nu_i=1" and MATHINLINE"\\nu P=\\nu". Shift the occupation count by one time step: times 0 through one before the return become times 1 through MATHINLINE"T_i"; both endpoints are MATHINLINE"i", so they cancel. All interchanges are initially nonnegative integrations.

In an irreducible recurrent chain each MATHINLINE"\\nu_j" is finite. From MATHINLINE"j" a positive-probability route hits MATHINLINE"i" before returning to MATHINLINE"j", so visits to MATHINLINE"j" before hitting MATHINLINE"i" are bounded by a geometric number with finite mean. If MATHINLINE"E_iT_i<\\infty", total mass is MATHINLINE"\\sum_j\\nu_j=E_iT_i", which normalizes to an invariant probability.
An invariant probability is thus more than a formal matrix eigenvector. It can be an actual return cycle's occupation budget divided by the cycle's mean length.

Conversely, suppose an irreducible countable chain has invariant probability MATHINLINE"\\pi". Start from a state of positive mass and propagate positivity along positive-probability paths using invariance; every MATHINLINE"\\pi_i>0". Under the stationary initial law, the events “at MATHINLINE"i" at time MATHINLINE"n", with no later visit” are disjoint for different MATHINLINE"n". Finite-block stationarity followed by a decreasing limit gives each probability MATHINLINE"\\pi_i(1-f_i)". Their infinite sum is at most one, forcing MATHINLINE"f_i=1" for every state. No general ergodic theorem has been used.

The remainder must actually vanish. By 18.9, every state MATHINLINE"k" hits MATHINLINE"i" almost surely: a positive-probability hitting path with no intermediate return to MATHINLINE"k" can be tried again at successive returns to MATHINLINE"k", and repeated failure has a geometric bound. Put MATHINLINE"H_i=\\inf\\{n\\ge0:X_n=i\\}" and MATHINLINE"D=E\\setminus\\{i\\}"; let MATHINLINE"K=(p_{k\\ell})_{k,\\ell\\in D}" be the substochastic matrix killed at MATHINLINE"i", and MATHINLINE"b=(p_{ij})_{j\\in D}". The invariant equation on MATHINLINE"D" gives
MATHBLOCK"\\pi_D=\\pi_i b+\\pi_DK\n=\\pi_i\\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}bK^r+\\pi_DK^N."

For MATHINLINE"j\\in D", MATHINLINE"\\sum_{r\\ge0}(bK^r)_j=\\nu_j": these are precisely the probabilities of visits after departure from MATHINLINE"i" and before its first return. The remainder has total mass
MATHBLOCK"\\sum_{j\\in D}(\\pi_DK^N)_j\n=\\sum_{k\\in D}\\pi_kP_k(H_i>N)\\longrightarrow0."

Every hitting tail tends to zero, dominated by the summable MATHINLINE"\\pi_k", so dominated convergence is justified. The first term tends to MATHINLINE"\\pi_i\\nu_j" by nonnegative monotone convergence. Include MATHINLINE"\\nu_i=1" and sum over all states to obtain
MATHBLOCK"\\pi_j=\\pi_i\\nu_j,\\qquad E_iT_i=1/\\pi_i."

Cycle budgets uniquely determine the invariant probability. Symmetric line walk is recurrent but, as Chapter 17 showed, has no invariant probability; it is null recurrent. Finite irreducible chains have invariant probabilities, hence positive recurrent states, though periodicity may still prevent stepwise convergence.

For a real random walk MATHINLINE"S_n" with independent identically distributed increments, let MATHINLINE"L" be the first strict ascent above the initial value and MATHINLINE"H=S_L". Their joint law may be defective: some paths never set a new high. Independent increments and stopping-time slices make the time and height increments between successive records have this same joint law.

If MATHINLINE"q(z,\\theta)=E[z^Le^{i\\theta H};L<\\infty]", with MATHINLINE"0\\le z<1", the sum of the joint transforms of all strict ascending records is MATHINLINE"\\sum_{k\\ge0}q(z,\\theta)^k=1/(1-q(z,\\theta))". Since MATHINLINE"|q(z,\\theta)|\\le z<1", absolute control justifies the summation. This proves the ladder renewal structure itself.

It is not yet the complete Wiener–Hopf factorization splitting the whole walk into ascending and descending parts. Strict-versus-weak boundary conventions and the full product identity still need a separate proof. This precise boundary is retained rather than declaring the entire discrete or Lévy factorization proved by naming it.

Unbiased steps cross a genuine boundary between dimensions two and three. The difference is not in one jump, but in the total budget for infinitely many possible returns. The Green sum records that budget; Fourier integration turns it into competition between singularity and volume near the origin.

Whenever a return occurs, the future begins from the same state again. A record is divided into cycles. Some never finish; others finish almost surely but have infinite mean. Combining these restarts to calculate long-term waiting requires more than deciding whether a return happens: it requires understanding how cycles fill time.

Pólya's paper, “Über eine Aufgabe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung betreffend die Irrfahrt im Straßennetz,” appeared in volume 84 of Mathematische Annalen in 1921, pages 149–160. The discounted Fourier argument here is a modern reconstruction using our established characteristic functions and integration tools, not a claim to reproduce his original proof. See the [original publication record](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01458701). The complete classification here concerns simple symmetric nearest-neighbor lattice walk; arbitrary jumps, dependent steps or general groups require proofs beyond a slogan about dimension.
一个人每次回到原点，都重新开始等待。若返回以后拥有同样的未来，那么一条漫长的记录可以不再按单步阅读，而按两次返回之间的周期阅读。
可是，在街边随意找一个时刻观察，看到的周期并不是随意抽取的一个周期。短周期很快就过去，长周期会占住更多的时间。一个完全没有预测能力的观察者，反而更容易落进较长的等待。
这两种阅读时间的方法——沿着到达次数数周期，沿着时间寻找自己所在的周期——将把同一份随机等待引向不同的概率。
设 MATHINLINE"X_1,X_2,\\ldots" 为独立同分布的严格正实随机变量，分布为 MATHINLINE"F"。令
MATHBLOCK"S_0=0,\\qquad S_n=X_1+\\cdots+X_n,\\qquad\nN(t)=\\max\\{n:S_n\\le t\\}."

称 MATHINLINE"S_n" 为更新时刻，MATHINLINE"N(t)" 为截至 MATHINLINE"t" 的更新次数，不计初始时刻。严格正性避免同一时刻堆积无限多个零周期。即使均值无穷，仍有 MATHINLINE"S_n\\to\\infty" 几乎必然：选 MATHINLINE"\\delta>0" 使 MATHINLINE"p=P(X_1\\ge\\delta)>0"，独立Bernoulli强律保证这样的间隔无穷多次出现。因此每个有限 MATHINLINE"t" 的计数有限。
这里用独立周期作模型；Markov链对一个常返状态的逐次返回，在首次返回之后正好提供这样的周期。暂留状态的缺失返回概率则必须先处理，不能把缺失质量当作一个有限等待间隔。
定义更新测度
MATHBLOCK"U(B)=\\sum_{n\\ge0}P(S_n\\in B),\\qquad U([0,t])=1+EN(t)."
选上节的 MATHINLINE"\\delta,p"。如果 MATHINLINE"S_n\\le h"，前 MATHINLINE"n" 次中，长度至少 MATHINLINE"\\delta" 的成功次数不超过 MATHINLINE"\\lfloor h/\\delta\\rfloor"。达到下一次成功所需的试验次数，是有限多个均值 MATHINLINE"1/p" 的几何等待之和。因此
MATHBLOCK"U([0,h])\\le\\frac{\\lfloor h/\\delta\\rfloor+1}{p}<\\infty."

更重要的是，对所有 MATHINLINE"t\\ge0"，MATHINLINE"U([t,t+h])\\le U([0,h])"。取首次进入 MATHINLINE"[t,\\infty)" 的更新时刻：若它已经越过右端，区间计数为0；否则，余下区间的访问数不超过一个从头开始、长度为 MATHINLINE"h" 的新更新过程所含的点数。按首次进入的下标分片，后续独立性证明这个期望上界。我们记统一界为 MATHINLINE"C_h"。它将负责后面所有不能只靠逐点极限完成的尾部控制。

但初等更新定理只估计一个越来越长区间中的平均点数，并不直接告诉我们最近一个短窗口里有多少点。要计算年龄、余寿命和延迟效应，需要真正的局部更新极限。

若存在最大的 MATHINLINE"d>0" 使 MATHINLINE"P(X_1\\in d\\mathbb Z)=1"，称更新间隔为算术型，跨度为 MATHINLINE"d"；否则称非算术型。这里是经过0的加法群，不是第十三章固定样本量的仿射格点跨度。支撑 MATHINLINE"\\{1,3\\}" 的更新跨度是1，虽然固定次数求和仍有奇偶限制；支撑 MATHINLINE"\\{1,\\sqrt2\\}" 的离散等待分布却是非算术型。
这个区别不会被无限次相加自动磨平。若每次间隔恰为1，观察时刻的相位将永远保留。非算术型的证明必须说明为什么不存在另一种隐蔽的周期，而不能把“没有密度”与“有周期”混为一谈。

先建立所需的专用工具。对于iid序列，若事件 MATHINLINE"A" 在任意有限坐标置换下都不变，则 MATHINLINE"P(A)" 为0或1。证明如下。第十五章的条件期望向上收敛，使 MATHINLINE"\\mathbf1_A" 可在 MATHINLINE"L^1" 中由有限前缀条件平均逼近；在1/2处截断，得到前 MATHINLINE"m" 个坐标中的事件 MATHINLINE"B"，满足 MATHINLINE"P(A\\triangle B)<\\varepsilon"。
给定任意有限前缀事件 MATHINLINE"C"，用一个有限置换把 MATHINLINE"B" 所用的坐标全移到 MATHINLINE"C" 之后。得到 MATHINLINE"B'" 与 MATHINLINE"C" 独立，且由iid对称性与 MATHINLINE"A" 不变性，仍有 MATHINLINE"P(A\\triangle B')<\\varepsilon"。因此
MATHBLOCK"|P(A\\cap C)-P(A)P(C)|\\le2\\varepsilon."
令ε趋0，再以π–λ把 MATHINLINE"C" 推广到整个序列σ-代数，MATHINLINE"A" 便与自身独立。对有界、有限置换不变的随机变量，把这一结论应用于全部有理水平集，便知它几乎必然为常数。这是本章实际需要的Hewitt–Savage型引理的完整证明，不借后文交换性或遍历理论。

设有界连续函数 MATHINLINE"h" 满足 MATHINLINE"h(t)=\\int h(t-x)F(dx)"。对固定 MATHINLINE"t"，MATHINLINE"h(t-S_n)" 是有界鞅，故有几乎必然及 MATHINLINE"L^1" 极限。任何有限置换最终不再改变部分和，因而不改变这个极限。上节说明极限是常数，其平均必为 MATHINLINE"h(t)"。闭鞅恒等式再推出 MATHINLINE"h(t-X_1)=h(t)" 几乎必然。
连续性把这个等式推广到支撑中的每个步长，并且对每个 MATHINLINE"t" 成立。于是 MATHINLINE"h" 对支撑生成的整个加法群不变。实线的加法子群若不是离散的 MATHINLINE"d\\mathbb Z"，就有任意小正元素，用整数倍逼近任意实数，故稠密。非算术时连续性迫使 MATHINLINE"h" 为常数。
在整数上，对有界函数与正整数步长，完全相同的鞅证明适用；若支撑的最大公约数为1，生成的群就是整个整数群，所以函数也是常数。这个调和机制是局部更新极限能够消除周期的真正原因。
将算术跨度缩放成1，记 MATHINLINE"u_n=U(\\{n\\})"，负下标取0。严格正整数间隔使同一条路径在一个点至多更新一次，所以 MATHINLINE"0\\le u_n\\le1"。更新递推为 MATHINLINE"u_n=\\mathbf1_{\\{n=0\\}}+\\sum_{k\\ge1}p_ku_{n-k}"。

MATHBLOCK"h(t)=\\int g(t-y)\\lambda(dy)"
有界连续，且满足19.7的调和方程。其有界性来自统一区间质量界，连续性来自 MATHINLINE"g" 的一致连续性与稍大支撑区间的质量界。故 MATHINLINE"h" 为常数。

还需确定 MATHINLINE"c"。每条路径的更新区间恰好覆盖时间轴，所以对 MATHINLINE"t\\ge0"，
MATHBLOCK"1=\\int_{[0,t]}\\overline F(t-s)U(ds),\\qquad \\overline F(x)=P(X_1>x)."
沿所选 MATHINLINE"t_j" 平移，在固定窗口 MATHINLINE"[-A,0]" 上，积分函数有界且单调，至多可数个跳跃；极限测度 MATHINLINE"c\\,dx" 没有这些点的质量，Riemann阶梯逼近便允许取极限。

这包括任意非算术严格正等待分布，不要求密度、二阶矩或spread-out条件。它也没有引用尚未建立的遍历定理。

这个结论来自最后周期的精确分片，不是把独立样本随便塞到随机时刻。算术情形沿固定相位使用19.11的求和版本；若周期恰为1，年龄就是观察时刻的小数部分，余寿命由同一相位决定。

沿到达点抽一个周期，每个周期只算一次；沿时间抽一个位置，每个周期按长度获得机会。相同的随机记录，因此能够产生两种不同的典型性。

到这里，重新开始仍是一条线：一个周期结束，下一个周期接上。若一次结束带来多个新的个体，每个个体又各自开始一次同样的实验，这条时间线便会分叉成一个家族。

Blackwell的1948年论文 [A renewal theorem](https://doi.org/10.1215/S0012-7094-48-01517-8)及1953年 [Extension of a renewal theorem](https://msp.org/pjm/1953/3-2/pjm-v3-n2-p03-p.pdf)是局部更新理论的重要原始来源。Smith的1958年综述 [Renewal Theory and its Ramifications](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1958.tb00294.x)讨论了更新与再生应用。本章的调和、置换与周期积分证明为现代重建；它处理严格正iid周期，不声称已经证明允许负增量的一般更新理论、遍历定理或Palm对偶。
Each return to the origin starts another wait. If return restores the same future, a long record can be read in cycles between returns rather than in single steps.

Yet a cycle encountered at an arbitrary roadside observation time is not a cycle chosen uniformly by its arrival index. Short cycles pass quickly; long ones occupy more time. An observer with no predictive knowledge is consequently more likely to land in a longer wait.
Counting cycles by arrivals and locating oneself by elapsed time assign different probabilities to the same random intervals.
Let MATHINLINE"X_1,X_2,\\ldots" be independent identically distributed strictly positive real variables with law MATHINLINE"F". Put
MATHBLOCK"S_0=0,\\qquad S_n=X_1+\\cdots+X_n,\\qquad\nN(t)=\\max\\{n:S_n\\le t\\}."

The MATHINLINE"S_n" are renewal times, and MATHINLINE"N(t)" counts renewals by MATHINLINE"t", excluding the initial point. Strict positivity prevents infinitely many zero-length cycles at one instant. Even with infinite mean, MATHINLINE"S_n\\to\\infty" almost surely: choose MATHINLINE"\\delta>0" with MATHINLINE"p=P(X_1\\ge\\delta)>0"; the independent Bernoulli strong law supplies infinitely many such intervals. Thus the count is finite for each finite MATHINLINE"t".

The model assumes independent cycles. Successive returns to a recurrent Markov state provide such cycles after the initial return. A transient state's missing return mass must be handled separately, not treated as a finite waiting interval.
Define the renewal measure
MATHBLOCK"U(B)=\\sum_{n\\ge0}P(S_n\\in B),\\qquad U([0,t])=1+EN(t)."

Choose the preceding MATHINLINE"\\delta,p". If MATHINLINE"S_n\\le h", at most MATHINLINE"\\lfloor h/\\delta\\rfloor" among the first MATHINLINE"n" intervals can be successes of length at least MATHINLINE"\\delta". The trial count needed for the next success is a sum of finitely many geometric waits of mean MATHINLINE"1/p". Hence
MATHBLOCK"U([0,h])\\le\\frac{\\lfloor h/\\delta\\rfloor+1}{p}<\\infty."

More importantly, for every MATHINLINE"t\\ge0", MATHINLINE"U([t,t+h])\\le U([0,h])". Consider the first renewal entering MATHINLINE"[t,\\infty)". If it overshoots the interval there are no points inside; otherwise the remaining count is no larger than the count in a fresh renewal process over length MATHINLINE"h". Split by the index of first entry and use independence of subsequent intervals to prove the expectation bound. Denote the common bound by MATHINLINE"C_h". It will control every tail passage for which pointwise convergence alone is inadequate.

Write MATHINLINE"\\mu=EX_1\\in(0,\\infty]". With finite mean, the strong law and MATHINLINE"S_{N(t)}\\le t<S_{N(t)+1}" give MATHINLINE"N(t)/t\\to1/\\mu" almost surely. With infinite mean, apply the strong law to every truncation MATHINLINE"X_k\\wedge a", then let MATHINLINE"a\\to\\infty", obtaining MATHINLINE"S_n/n\\to\\infty". The same conclusion holds with MATHINLINE"1/\\infty=0".

Convergence of mean counts needs another argument. Set MATHINLINE"\\mu_a=E(X_1\\wedge a)". The event MATHINLINE"\\{N(t)+1\\ge k\\}=\\{S_{k-1}\\le t\\}" is independent of the next interval, so Tonelli gives
MATHBLOCK"\\mu_a E[N(t)+1]\n=E\\sum_{k=1}^{N(t)+1}(X_k\\wedge a)\\le t+a."

Section 19.2 ensures finiteness; truncation bounds the last crossing interval by MATHINLINE"a". Thus MATHINLINE"\\limsup EN(t)/t\\le1/\\mu_a". Let MATHINLINE"a\\to\\infty" and use Fatou for the opposite lower bound to prove the elementary renewal theorem:
MATHBLOCK"\\frac{EN(t)}t\\longrightarrow\\frac1\\mu."
This is more careful than formally substituting a random index into an expectation. Pathwise rate comes first, and a bounded overshoot budget supplies the mean rate.
The renewal measure satisfies MATHINLINE"U=\\delta_0+F*U". For a function MATHINLINE"g", write MATHINLINE"(U*g)(t)=\\int_{[0,t]}g(t-s)U(ds)". Whenever the absolute convolution is finite, it solves
MATHBLOCK"z(t)=g(t)+\\int_{(0,t]}z(t-x)F(dx)."

This is the renewal equation. Successive substitution produces MATHINLINE"g+F*g+F^{*2}*g+\\cdots". For locally bounded MATHINLINE"g", 19.2 ensures absolute convergence on bounded time intervals. The solution is unique in the same locally bounded class: after iteration the remainder is bounded by MATHINLINE"P(S_n\\le t)" times a local bound, and this probability tends to zero.

The elementary renewal theorem concerns an average over a growing interval. It does not directly count renewals in a short recent window. Age, remaining lifetime and delay require a genuine local renewal limit.

The waiting law is arithmetic with span MATHINLINE"d" if MATHINLINE"d>0" is the largest number with MATHINLINE"P(X_1\\in d\\mathbb Z)=1"; otherwise it is nonarithmetic. This is an additive group through zero, not Chapter 13's affine lattice span for a fixed number of summands. Support MATHINLINE"\\{1,3\\}" has renewal span 1 despite parity restrictions at fixed sample size. The discrete waiting law on MATHINLINE"\\{1,\\sqrt2\\}" is nonarithmetic.

Infinite addition does not automatically erase this distinction. With every interval equal to 1, observation phase persists forever. The nonarithmetic proof must exclude hidden periodicity rather than confusing lack of density with presence of a period.

We first prove the special tool required. For an iid sequence, an event MATHINLINE"A" invariant under every finite coordinate permutation has probability MATHINLINE"P(A)" equal to zero or one. Chapter 15's upward conditional-expectation theorem approximates MATHINLINE"\\mathbf1_A" in MATHINLINE"L^1" by finite-prefix conditional averages. Threshold at one half to obtain an event MATHINLINE"B" in the first MATHINLINE"m" coordinates with MATHINLINE"P(A\\triangle B)<\\varepsilon".

For any finite-prefix event MATHINLINE"C", use a finite permutation moving all coordinates of MATHINLINE"B" beyond those of MATHINLINE"C". The resulting MATHINLINE"B'" is independent of MATHINLINE"C", and iid symmetry together with invariance of MATHINLINE"A" still gives MATHINLINE"P(A\\triangle B')<\\varepsilon". Therefore
MATHBLOCK"|P(A\\cap C)-P(A)P(C)|\\le2\\varepsilon."

Let epsilon vanish, then extend MATHINLINE"C" to the full sequence sigma-field by pi–lambda. The event MATHINLINE"A" is independent of itself. Applied to all rational level sets of a bounded permutation-invariant variable, this makes the variable almost surely constant. This proves the needed Hewitt–Savage-type lemma without importing later exchangeability or ergodic theory.

Let bounded continuous MATHINLINE"h" satisfy MATHINLINE"h(t)=\\int h(t-x)F(dx)". For fixed MATHINLINE"t", the variables MATHINLINE"h(t-S_n)" form a bounded martingale, with an almost sure and MATHINLINE"L^1" limit. A finite permutation eventually leaves partial sums unchanged, hence leaves that limit unchanged. The preceding lemma makes the limit constant, with mean MATHINLINE"h(t)". The closed-martingale identity then forces MATHINLINE"h(t-X_1)=h(t)" almost surely.

Continuity extends the identity to every step in the support, for each MATHINLINE"t". Thus MATHINLINE"h" is invariant under the additive group generated by the support. A subgroup of the line that is not a discrete MATHINLINE"d\\mathbb Z" contains arbitrarily small positive elements; integer multiples approximate any real number, so the group is dense. Nonarithmeticity and continuity force MATHINLINE"h" to be constant.

For a bounded function on the integers and positive integer increments, the same martingale proof applies. If the support has greatest common divisor one, it generates the entire integer group, and the function is constant there. This harmonic mechanism explains how the local renewal limit removes periodic oscillation.

Rescale arithmetic span to 1. Put MATHINLINE"u_n=U(\\{n\\})", zero at negative indices. Strictly positive integer intervals allow at most one renewal at any point of a path, so MATHINLINE"0\\le u_n\\le1". The renewal recursion is MATHINLINE"u_n=\\mathbf1_{\\{n=0\\}}+\\sum_{k\\ge1}p_ku_{n-k}".

From any integer sequence tending to infinity, extract a subsequence simultaneously for every fixed integer offset so that MATHINLINE"u_{n_j+\\ell}\\to v(\\ell)". Domination by 1 passes the recursion through the sum, giving MATHINLINE"v(\\ell)=\\sum_kp_kv(\\ell-k)". The integer harmonic lemma makes MATHINLINE"v\\equiv c".
Exactly one renewal cycle contains each time, yielding the identity
MATHBLOCK"1=\\sum_{k=0}^nP(X_1>k)u_{n-k}."

With finite mean, the tail weights sum to MATHINLINE"\\mu". Truncation followed by the bound 1 controls the remainder, giving MATHINLINE"1=c\\mu". Every subsequence has this same limit, hence MATHINLINE"u_n\\to1/\\mu". Restoring span gives MATHINLINE"d/\\mu". We have identified mass at individual allowable renewal points, rather than only an averaged cycle rate.

The nonarithmetic conclusions here through 19.11 assume strictly positive iid intervals, a nonarithmetic law and MATHINLINE"0<\\mu<\\infty"; the arithmetic case separately retains its phase. Extend MATHINLINE"U" by zero on the negative half-line. For any MATHINLINE"t_j\\to\\infty", write MATHINLINE"U_t(B)=U(t+B)". The uniform local bound in 19.2 gives a subsequence of these translated measures converging against continuous compactly supported test functions to a locally finite measure MATHINLINE"\\lambda". [T-STIELTJES](../foundations/t-stieltjes.md#t-stieltjes-selection) proves this selection through rational diagonal extraction, monotone functions and a pushforward of level-axis length.

Write MATHINLINE"U_t(g)=\\int g(y)U_t(dy)". The translated renewal equation is MATHINLINE"U_t(g)=g(-t)+\\int U_t(g(\\,\\cdot+x))F(dx)", fixing the direction of translation. If the support of MATHINLINE"g" lies in an interval of length MATHINLINE"H", every inner absolute integral is at most MATHINLINE"\\|g\\|_\\infty C_H", uniformly in MATHINLINE"x,t". For each fixed MATHINLINE"x" the translated test function is still continuous and compactly supported. Pass to the subsequential limit and then use this common bound under the probability MATHINLINE"F", together with MATHINLINE"g(-t_j)\\to0", to obtain MATHINLINE"\\lambda=F*\\lambda". More explicitly, for any continuous compactly supported MATHINLINE"g", the function
MATHBLOCK"h(t)=\\int g(t-y)\\lambda(dy)"

is bounded and continuous and satisfies the harmonic equation of 19.7. The uniform interval bound gives boundedness; uniform continuity of MATHINLINE"g" and the mass bound on a slightly enlarged support give continuity. Thus MATHINLINE"h" is constant.

It follows that MATHINLINE"\\lambda" is translation invariant: every test function has equal integrals under every translate. Approximate intervals from inside and outside by continuous piecewise linear functions to obtain equality of translated interval masses. Point masses must vanish, since arbitrarily many distinct translates of an atom would violate local finiteness. Interval mass therefore depends only on length, is additive and monotone in length. Establish linearity for rational lengths, then squeeze real lengths between rationals. Consequently MATHINLINE"\\lambda=c\\,dx".
It remains to find MATHINLINE"c". Each path's renewal intervals partition the time axis, so for MATHINLINE"t\\ge0",
MATHBLOCK"1=\\int_{[0,t]}\\overline F(t-s)U(ds),\\qquad \\overline F(x)=P(X_1>x)."

Translate along the selected MATHINLINE"t_j". On a fixed window MATHINLINE"[-A,0]", the integrand is bounded and monotone, with at most countably many jumps. The limit measure MATHINLINE"c\\,dx" gives them no mass, so Riemann step approximation allows passage to the limit.
Outside that window, merely writing DCT would be insufficient. For fixed mesh MATHINLINE"h>0", the uniform local bound controls the tail by
MATHBLOCK"C_h\\sum_{k\\ge\\lfloor A/h\\rfloor-1}\\overline F(kh)."

Finite mean makes the decreasing tail function integrable, so this fixed-mesh tail sum vanishes. Therefore MATHINLINE"1=c\\int_0^\\infty\\overline F(x)dx=c\\mu". All subsequential candidates coincide, proving the full local renewal limit
MATHBLOCK"U((t,t+h])\\longrightarrow h/\\mu\\qquad(h>0)."
This covers every strictly positive nonarithmetic waiting law with finite mean, without density, second-moment or spread-out assumptions. No unproved ergodic theorem has entered.

Extend MATHINLINE"g" by zero on negative arguments. It is directly Riemann integrable if its positive and negative parts have mesh upper and lower sums converging to the same finite values as the mesh vanishes, and its absolute-value upper sum is finite for a sufficiently fine fixed mesh. This controls both local oscillation and distant spikes. Mere Lebesgue integrability does not control sampling by the renewal measure at particular time points.

For compactly supported Riemann-integrable functions, the interval limit of 19.10 and step bounds first give the convolution limit. For general MATHINLINE"g", the fixed-mesh far convolution tail is bounded by MATHINLINE"C_h" times the corresponding upper-envelope tail sum; it vanishes as the truncation bound MATHINLINE"A\\to\\infty", uniformly over observation times MATHINLINE"t\\ge0". Truncate, take the long-time limit, then enlarge the truncation. This proves the nonarithmetic key renewal theorem:
MATHBLOCK"\\int_{[0,t]}g(t-s)U(ds)\\longrightarrow\\frac1\\mu\\int_0^\\infty g(s)ds."

For arithmetic span MATHINLINE"d", a sum cannot be replaced by an integral. At fixed phase MATHINLINE"r\\in[0,d)", if the sampled sequence is absolutely summable, 19.8 and the bound MATHINLINE"u_n\\le1" give
MATHBLOCK"(U*g)(nd+r)\\longrightarrow\\frac d\\mu\\sum_{k\\ge0}g(kd+r)."

Direct Riemann integrability guarantees this summability. Unit deterministic periods and a narrow window function already show why removing phase can destroy existence of a common limit. Another counterexample concerns integrability itself: let MATHINLINE"g=\\mathbf1_{\\mathbb N_0}". Its Lebesgue integral is zero, yet at every integer time the initial renewal point alone contributes at least one to the convolution. This function is not directly Riemann integrable. Even a nonarithmetic waiting law therefore does not make ordinary Lebesgue integrability sufficient.

Allow cycles to carry rewards, with iid pairs MATHINLINE"(X_k,R_k)", MATHINLINE"E|R_1|<\\infty" and MATHINLINE"\\mu<\\infty". Reward and duration within a cycle may be dependent. Completed-cycle reward satisfies
MATHBLOCK"\\frac1t\\sum_{k=1}^{N(t)}R_k\n=\\frac{N(t)}t\\frac1{N(t)}\\sum_{k=1}^{N(t)}R_k\n\\longrightarrow\\frac{ER_1}{\\mu}\\quad\\text{a.s.}"

This applies a strong law along a random subsequence already tending to infinity; MATHINLINE"N(t)" need not be independent of rewards. If absolute accrued reward in an unfinished cycle is bounded by its MATHINLINE"V_k", where MATHINLINE"(X_k,R_k,V_k)" are iid and MATHINLINE"EV_1<\\infty", tail-integral comparison and Borel–Cantelli give MATHINLINE"V_k/k\\to0" almost surely. Hence MATHINLINE"V_{N(t)+1}/t\\to0", and reward accrued continuously within a cycle has the same limit.
This renewal reward theorem is pathwise. Convergence of expectations would require suitable additional control such as uniform integrability; the strong law alone does not authorize it.

Define age MATHINLINE"A_t=t-S_{N(t)}" and residual life MATHINLINE"R_t=S_{N(t)+1}-t". For MATHINLINE"a,b\\ge0", splitting by the last renewal expresses the probability of MATHINLINE"A_t>a,R_t>b" as the integral of MATHINLINE"\\overline F(t+b-s)" over MATHINLINE"s<t-a". Its forcing function MATHINLINE"g(u)=\\mathbf1_{\\{u>a\\}}\\overline F(u+b)" is piecewise monotone and integrable, hence directly Riemann integrable.
In the nonarithmetic finite-mean case, the key renewal theorem gives
MATHBLOCK"P(A_t>a,R_t>b)\\longrightarrow\n\\frac1\\mu\\int_{a+b}^\\infty\\overline F(u)du\n=\\frac{E(X_1-a-b)^+}{\\mu}."

This comes from an exact last-cycle decomposition rather than inserting an independent sample at a random time. In the arithmetic case use the phase-dependent sum of 19.11. If every cycle has length 1, age is the observation time's fractional part and residual life is fixed by the same phase.

Construct the limiting joint law by first taking length-biased MATHINLINE"L", with MATHINLINE"P(L\\in dx)=xF(dx)/\\mu", then independent MATHINLINE"V\\sim\\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)", and setting age to MATHINLINE"VL", residual to MATHINLINE"(1-V)L". Given the length, positions satisfying both inequalities occupy length MATHINLINE"(L-a-b)^+". Integration under the length-biased law recovers 19.13.

This is the inspection paradox: the observer learns no hidden fact, but longer intervals occupy more time. The deterministic sample in the figure displays this weighting without replacing the infinite renewal proof.

With finite second moment, the encountered whole interval has mean MATHINLINE"EX_1^2/\\mu"; age and residual each have mean MATHINLINE"EX_1^2/(2\\mu)". With infinite second moment these remain extended nonnegative integral identities. It would be wrong to conclude that residual life always exceeds the mean ordinary whole interval: for a constant interval it is half that length. What is necessarily length-biased is the entire interval encountered by the observer.

The same ten intervals produce different length distributions under uniform interval sampling and uniform time observation. Lengths 1, 2 and 5 occur 6, 2 and 2 times: their event weights are 0.6, 0.2 and 0.2, but their time weights are 0.3, 0.2 and 0.5. Longer intervals occupy more time, raising the mean containing-interval length from 2 to 3.2. This deterministic illustration on a total length of 20 is not a proof of stationary renewal construction or a renewal limit theorem. Containing-interval length is not residual life.

Take bilateral iid intervals and root a renewal point at zero, obtaining a locally finite configuration MATHINLINE"\\Phi" on both sides. Use only the sigma-field generated by counts in bounded intervals, without assuming general point-process or Palm theory. Let MATHINLINE"\\theta_s" move the observation origin to MATHINLINE"s". Length-bias the central interval, place the origin uniformly inside it, and append independent ordinary intervals in both directions. This constructs a probability MATHINLINE"Q" satisfying, for every bounded measurable configuration function MATHINLINE"H",
MATHBLOCK"QH=\\frac1\\mu E\\int_0^{X_1}H(\\theta_s\\Phi)ds."
This gives more than an age-residual pair: it makes the entire configuration stationary. For MATHINLINE"t>0", the exact difference of translated integration intervals is
MATHBLOCK"\\mu\\{Q(H\\circ\\theta_t)-QH\\}\n=E\\int_{X_1}^{X_1+t}H(\\theta_u\\Phi)du\n-E\\int_0^tH(\\theta_u\\Phi)du=0."

Moving the point root from 0 to the next renewal at MATHINLINE"X_1" merely reindexes the bilateral iid intervals, preserving their joint law. Both final integrals have fixed length MATHINLINE"t", so boundedness ensures integrability. Negative shifts follow by inverse composition. This proves stationarity rather than guessing a stationary residual density. With arithmetic intervals, stationarity under all real shifts also randomizes the grid phase through the uniform interior location; fixed-grid observations retain their discrete phase version.

If MATHINLINE"P(X_1>x)=(1+x)^{-\\alpha}", MATHINLINE"0<\\alpha<1", every interval is still finite and renewals occur indefinitely, but MATHINLINE"EN(t)/t\\to0" and MATHINLINE"N(t)/t\\to0" almost surely. There is no probability obtained by normalizing MATHINLINE"xF(dx)" with a finite MATHINLINE"\\mu"; age and residual cannot use 19.13's finite-mean equilibrium formula.

Cycles still fill the time axis, but a finite mean cycle no longer supplies a normalizing budget. This does not say every infinite-mean limit is impossible. It identifies exactly why the stationary length bias and finite-mean limits in this chapter need their hypotheses.
Sampling by arrivals counts every cycle once. Sampling by time gives every cycle weight proportional to length. The same random record therefore admits two different notions of a typical observation.

The strong law gives the average pace, the local renewal limit stabilizes short windows, and length bias explains the observer's longer interval. All depend on restart structure, but each needs its own tail, periodicity and integrability assumptions.
So far restarts form a line: one cycle ends and the next follows. If one ending produces several new individuals, each beginning the same experiment independently, the line branches into a family.

Blackwell's 1948 [A renewal theorem](https://doi.org/10.1215/S0012-7094-48-01517-8) and 1953 [Extension of a renewal theorem](https://msp.org/pjm/1953/3-2/pjm-v3-n2-p03-p.pdf) are original sources for local renewal theory. Smith's 1958 survey [Renewal Theory and its Ramifications](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1958.tb00294.x) discusses renewal and regenerative applications. The harmonic, permutation and cycle-integral proofs here are modern reconstructions for strictly positive iid cycles. They do not establish renewal theory for general signed increments, an ergodic theorem or Palm duality.
一个家族有时只延续几代，有时不断分出新的支系。如果每个人的后代数遵从同一份随机规则，平均每个人留下两个后代，能否说这个家族的未来已经安全？
平均人口确实可以指数增长。但一个没有后代的祖先，不会因为别的家族繁荣而重新出现。期望把许多可能的世界放在一起；生存却属于某一棵真正长出来的树。
十九世纪关于姓氏消失的提问曾把这种差别带到数学面前。这里保留它提出问题的力量，但采用一个明确的现代模型：个体、世代和独立的生育规则，不把简化模型等同于真实人口史。
令 MATHINLINE"L" 为非负整数值后代数，MATHINLINE"p_k=P(L=k)"。以一个祖先开始，每个已经出生的个体独立产生一份 MATHINLINE"L"。用所有有限正整数词标记潜在个体：空词是根，词后接 MATHINLINE"j" 表示它的第 MATHINLINE"j" 个孩子。这个集合可数，第八章的乘积空间或第十七章的顺序构造提供全部后代实验。
保留那些沿祖先链每一项孩子下标都不超过相应后代数的词。每一代只有有限个个体，因为每个后代数有限，有限个有限数之和仍有限。记第 MATHINLINE"n" 代人口为 MATHINLINE"Z_n"，则
MATHBLOCK"Z_0=1,\\qquad Z_{n+1}=\\sum_{j=1}^{Z_n}L_{n,j}."
这就是Galton–Watson过程。滤过 MATHINLINE"\\mathcal F_n" 揭示截至第 MATHINLINE"n" 代的树，但尚未揭示该代个体的后代数。这个时机决定哪些生育实验仍然独立于过去。
定义后代概率母函数
MATHBLOCK"f(s)=E s^L=\\sum_{k\\ge0}p_ks^k,\\qquad0\\le s\\le1,"
其中 MATHINLINE"0^0=1"。给定当前人口，独立性给出 MATHINLINE"E[s^{Z_{n+1}}\\mid\\mathcal F_n]=f(s)^{Z_n}"。因此第 MATHINLINE"n" 代人口母函数为 MATHINLINE"f^{\\circ n}(s)"，这里是函数复合，不是普通的幂。
对不同个体的后代相乘，再逐代复合，正是谱系中两种独立结构的区别。从 MATHINLINE"r" 个祖先出发，整个家族是 MATHINLINE"r" 棵独立树之和，母函数相应为 MATHINLINE"(f^{\\circ n}(s))^r"。

记 MATHINLINE"q_n=P(Z_n=0)=f^{\\circ n}(0)"。零人口一旦出现就不会恢复，所以 MATHINLINE"q_n\\uparrow q"，而 MATHINLINE"q" 正是最终灭绝概率。MATHINLINE"f" 在 MATHINLINE"[0,1]" 连续，由有界收敛得到 MATHINLINE"f(q)=q"。若 MATHINLINE"s\\in[0,1]" 是任何不动点，从0开始迭代的单调性给出 MATHINLINE"q_n\\le s"，故 MATHINLINE"q\\le s"。因此
MATHBLOCK"q=\\min\\{s\\in[0,1]:f(s)=s\\}."
这不是只解一个方程再任选一个根。由有限代灭绝概率出发，决定了为什么必须选择最小根。从多个祖先出发的灭绝概率为 MATHINLINE"q^r"，直接来自独立家族分解。
以下取有限均值 MATHINLINE"m=EL"。若 MATHINLINE"m=0"，下一代立即灭绝。对 MATHINLINE"m>0"，MATHINLINE"f" 非降且凸，左导数 MATHINLINE"f'(1)=m"，这由非负级数单调收敛得到。

若 MATHINLINE"m<1"，则对 MATHINLINE"s<1"，MATHINLINE"f(s)-s>0"：其导数不超过 MATHINLINE"m-1<0"，而在1为0。若 MATHINLINE"m=1" 且 MATHINLINE"P(L=1)<1"，均值条件迫使有正概率取0与至少2，严格凸性使 MATHINLINE"f(s)>s" 对 MATHINLINE"s<1" 成立。这两种情形都只有不动点1，故几乎必然灭绝。

例外 MATHINLINE"L\\equiv1" 必须单列：每代恰有一个人，永不灭绝。当 MATHINLINE"m>1" 时，MATHINLINE"f(s)-s" 在接近1的左侧为负，在0非负，因此存在 MATHINLINE"q<1"。严格凸性保证不动点只有 MATHINLINE"q,1"。若 MATHINLINE"p_0=0"，最小根为0；否则 MATHINLINE"0<q<1"。这就是次临界、临界与超临界分类的准确范围。
条件平均为 MATHINLINE"E[Z_{n+1}\\mid\\mathcal F_n]=mZ_n"，所以 MATHINLINE"EZ_n=m^n"。例如 MATHINLINE"p_0=1/4,p_2=3/4"，均值为 MATHINLINE"3/2"，但不动点方程给出 MATHINLINE"q=1/3"。平均人口不断增加，仍有三分之一的家族消失。
在临界例子 MATHINLINE"p_0=p_2=1/2" 中，平均人口始终为1，却几乎必然最终灭绝。第十五章中公平但归零的本钱，在这里有了亲缘结构：极少数很大的家族承载平均值，而多数记录已经终止。
对 MATHINLINE"m>0"，令 MATHINLINE"W_n=Z_n/m^n"。它是均值为1的非负鞅，所以第十五章保证几乎必然收敛到有限的 MATHINLINE"W"，且 MATHINLINE"EW\\le1"。我们还不知道它是否丢掉期望，更不知道在生存的家族上 MATHINLINE"W" 是否为正。
若超临界并且 MATHINLINE"\\sigma^2=\\operatorname{Var}L<\\infty"，全方差公式给出
MATHBLOCK"\\operatorname{Var}(W_n)=\\frac{\\sigma^2}{m(m-1)}(1-m^{-n})."

A family sometimes lasts only a few generations and sometimes keeps producing new branches. If every individual's offspring count follows the same random rule, with two children on average, is the family's future secure?

Mean population can indeed grow exponentially. But an ancestor without children does not return because other families prosper. Expectation combines many possible worlds; survival belongs to one tree that actually grows.

Nineteenth-century questions about disappearing surnames brought this distinction before mathematics. We retain their motivating question while specifying a modern model of individuals, generations and independent reproduction, rather than equating it with actual population history.

Let MATHINLINE"L" be a nonnegative integer offspring count with MATHINLINE"p_k=P(L=k)". Begin with one ancestor, and give every born individual an independent copy of MATHINLINE"L". Label potential individuals by finite words of positive integers: the empty word is the root, and appending MATHINLINE"j" identifies the MATHINLINE"j"th child. The label set is countable, so Chapter 8's product space or Chapter 17's sequential construction provides all reproduction experiments.

Keep the words whose child labels along every ancestral step do not exceed the corresponding offspring counts. Each generation is finite because each offspring count is finite and a finite sum of finite numbers remains finite. Writing MATHINLINE"Z_n" for generation MATHINLINE"n",
MATHBLOCK"Z_0=1,\\qquad Z_{n+1}=\\sum_{j=1}^{Z_n}L_{n,j}."

MATHBLOCK"f(s)=E s^L=\\sum_{k\\ge0}p_ks^k,\\qquad0\\le s\\le1,"
